title: feat: maintenance mode with bypass link (replaces Hostinger Tools maintenance mode)
body:
## Why

Hostinger Tools (`hostinger` on WordPress.org) is installed on some managed sites mainly for its maintenance mode. It is often out of date and adds a host-specific dependency. A small maintenance mode in SEO Pro Stack lets those sites drop it.

(Brief refreshed 2026-10-02: the original paths predate the v0.3 rewrite. Follow the current pattern below.)

## What

A **Maintenance mode** feature, off by default (repo rule: features are off by default):

- When on, logged-out visitors get a `503` with `Retry-After` and a minimal, translatable page (site name + message), `noindex`. Use `wp_die()`-style output or a small template; it must follow the Kadence light/dark rules in `AGENTS.md` → Front-end styling if it carries any styles (prefer none: `currentColor`/system colours).
- People who can `manage_options` (filterable, e.g. `seoprostack_maintenance_capability`) see the site normally, plus an admin-bar notice ("Maintenance mode is on") linking to the setting.
- Child settings (`'parent' => self::KEY`): message text, and a **bypass link**: a random token; visiting `/?seoprostack-bypass=<token>` sets an HttpOnly, Secure (on HTTPS), SameSite=Lax cookie for 24 h whose value is an HMAC of the token (`wp_hash()`), so regenerating the token invalidates old links and cookies. Show the link with a "New link" action (nonce + capability check).
- Never block `wp-login.php`, `wp-admin`, `admin-ajax.php`, REST requests from logged-in users, WP-CLI, cron, `robots.txt` or the sitemap.
- **Replaces** Hostinger Tools' maintenance mode: `'replaces' => array('hostinger' => 'Hostinger Tools')` and import its setting in `migrate()` with `self::import_setting()` (fills only unset keys). Find Hostinger Tools' option names in its current source (WordPress.org SVN `https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/hostinger/trunk/`, or the plugin API); if no setting can be mapped, say so in the PR. Hostinger Tools does more than this (auto-updates, XML-RPC and other switches, see #3), so add the rest to the `seoprostack_replaced_plugin_extras` filter if it exists on `main` (PR #131 adds it), so the Plugins screen does not tell people it can go.

## Files to modify

- NEW `includes/features/class-seoprostack-maintenance.php` — extend `SEOProStack_Feature` (`includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php`); `settings()` schema, `boot()` returns early unless `self::enabled()`. Model on `includes/features/class-seoprostack-gone-urls.php` (front-end request handling, `replaces`, child settings).
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php` — register in `SEOProStack::$core_features`.
- `uninstall.php` — remove the token option (and anything else new).
- `admin/data/free-plugins.php` — remove `hostinger` if listed, with a comment (it is not listed today; check).
- `README.md` (feature section, Features table row for the replaced plugin, Credits row: plugin, maker, its WordPress.org page and maker's source repo checked with `gh api` or the plugin API, never guessed; hooks; changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (one short line; stay under 10 KB — `scripts/preflight-release.sh` reports the size).

## Verification

Per `AGENTS.md` → Testing, on a throwaway Docker WordPress site (never the shared preview site): `php -l` changed files; turn the feature on; logged-out `curl -i` the home page → 503 + `Retry-After` + `noindex`; `wp-login.php`, `/wp-json/` with a logged-in cookie, `robots.txt` and WP-CLI still work; the bypass link sets the cookie and shows the site; "New link" invalidates the old cookie; admin bar notice shows for admins; Hostinger Tools import on a site with its option seeded (delete `seoprostack_options` and `seoprostack_db_version` while inactive, then activate); no new `seoprostack` messages in `debug.log`. Smoke-test on WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 (`wordpress:php7.4-apache`). Run `scripts/build-release.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` and `scripts/plugin-check.sh`. Push and open the PR; the owner reviews on the combined preview (`scripts/preview-site.sh`).

title: feat: security toggles to disable XML-RPC and application passwords (replaces Hostinger Tools security)
body:
## Why

The other reason some managed sites keep Hostinger Tools (`hostinger` on WordPress.org) is two hardening switches, which Disable Bloat also has. Both take a few lines with core filters; moving them into SEO Pro Stack removes a host-specific plugin and closes two of the gaps the Plugins screen names for Disable Bloat.

(Brief refreshed 2026-10-02: the original paths predate the v0.3 rewrite. Follow the current pattern below.)

## Depends on

PR #131 (#122) adds `includes/class-seoprostack-disable-bloat.php`, whose `MAP` imports Disable Bloat settings and whose `names()`/`uncovered()` list `xml_rpc_disable` and `app_passwords_disable` as not covered. If it is merged when you start, wire these switches into it (import + drop them from the uncovered list). If it is not, build the feature without that and say in the PR that the Disable Bloat mapping follows once #131 merges.

## What

One feature, off by default, with two switches (both off by default):

- **Turn off XML-RPC**: `add_filter('xmlrpc_enabled', '__return_false')`, drop the `X-Pingback` header (`wp_headers`) and the RSD link (`remove_action('wp_head', 'rsd_link')`), and answer direct `xmlrpc.php` requests with `403`. The description says Jetpack and some mobile apps need XML-RPC.
- **Turn off application passwords**: `add_filter('wp_is_application_passwords_available', '__return_false')` (also hides the profile section and the "Authorize application" screen).
- `SEOProStack_Feature::enabled()` reads only `KEY`; read the second switch with `SEOProStack_Settings::get('…')` in `boot()`, or make both child settings of one card — follow an existing feature with child settings (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-avatar-privacy.php`).
- **Replaces** Hostinger Tools' two switches: `'replaces' => array('hostinger' => 'Hostinger Tools')`, imported in `migrate()` with `self::import_setting()`. Find its option names in its current source (WordPress.org SVN `https://plugins.svn.wordpress.org/hostinger/trunk/`); if none map, say so in the PR. Coordinate with #2 (maintenance mode also replaces Hostinger Tools): whichever lands second extends, not duplicates, the extras list.

## Files to modify

- NEW `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hardening.php` — extends `SEOProStack_Feature`; schema in `settings()`; `boot()` returns early unless enabled.
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php` — register in `SEOProStack::$core_features`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-disable-bloat.php` — only if #131 is merged (see above).
- `README.md` (feature section, Features table, Credits for Hostinger Tools if not already added by #2: plugin, maker, WordPress.org page and the maker's own source repo, checked with `gh api`/plugin API, never guessed; changelog), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (one short line; under 10 KB).

## Verification

Per `AGENTS.md` → Testing on a throwaway Docker WordPress site: `php -l`; with the switch on, `curl -i -X POST <site>/xmlrpc.php` → 403, no `X-Pingback` header and no RSD link on the home page; with application passwords off, the profile section is gone and `wp-admin/authorize-application.php` refuses; both off → everything as before; imports from seeded Hostinger Tools (and Disable Bloat, if wired) options with `seoprostack_options`/`seoprostack_db_version` deleted while inactive; no new `seoprostack` messages in `debug.log`; WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 smoke test; `scripts/build-release.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`. Push and open the PR; the owner reviews on the combined preview (`scripts/preview-site.sh`).

title: feat: replace more plugins with SEO Pro Stack features and speed up wp-admin
body:
## Goal

Replace more single-purpose plugins with opt-in SEO Pro Stack features, reorganise the settings navigation for the larger feature set, and work towards a wp-admin that stays fast with 200 plugins.

Every feature follows `AGENTS.md`:
- one class in `includes/features/`, extending `SEOProStack_Feature`, off by default
- `'replaces' => array(slug => name)`, with a one-time settings import in `migrate()`
- the slug removed from `admin/data/free-plugins.php`
- cleanup in `uninstall.php`
- `README.md` and `readme.txt` updated in the same PR

## Evidence (read-only survey of the Hostinger account, 2026-09-30)

- **Pretty Links:** live links on client-c.example (87 links, 6,590 clicks), client-b.example (12), client-e.example (3), wpallstars.com (3), client-f.example (2), client-a.example (1) and one staging site (1).
  - Used: slug (some start `link/`), target URL, redirect type 301/307, nofollow, sponsored, click tracking and categories.
  - Stored but to be confirmed unused before migrating: split tests, expiry and dynamic redirects.
- **Spectra on client-a.example:** 16 posts use it. Published content uses `uagb/image` (3 pages), `uagb/taxonomy-list` (`awards-programmes`), `uagb/advanced-heading` (2 posts) and `uagb/buttons` (4 posts).
- **Hide Admin Notices, Plugin Toggle, CompressX, The Paste, Avatar Privacy, Easy Watermark, Enable Media Replace, Imsanity, Safe SVG, Index WP MySQL For Speed, Remove CPT base:** each is active on several of the sites.

## Phases

Each line ends with the merged PR that delivered it (`For #7`). Follow-up PRs and issues are listed under it.

- Phase 1: Navigation, settings tabs regrouped by area with a feature search #8
  - Files: `admin/includes/class-admin-manager.php`, each feature's `'tab'`, `admin/js`, `admin/css`. Feature search placement fixed in #27.
- Phase 2: Plugins screen, toggles, plugin sizes and deleted plugin cleanup #9
  - Toggle switches with a confirmation that names the plugin (replaces Plugin Toggle).
  - A plugin weight column showing PHP, JS, CSS, media and other file sizes.
  - Repair of "plugin file does not exist" leftovers (replaces the maintainer's `wp-fix-plugin-does-not-exist-notices`). Plugin Check fix in #10.
- Phase 3: Admin, hide notices, paste media and avatar privacy #13
  - Hide admin notices (replaces Hide Admin Notices): #11, with follow-ups #14, #24, #29 and #49.
  - The Paste: #12.
  - Avatar privacy (replaces Avatar Privacy): #13.
  - Disable WordPress updates: dropped by decision. Plugin Check reports `plugin_updater_detected`, and it would also hide updates from GitHub releases (#167). Parked on `feature/disable-updates-parked`.
- Phase 4: Media 1, SVG uploads, resize large uploads and replace media #15
  - Resize large uploads with a bulk pass (replaces Imsanity), sanitised SVG uploads (replaces Safe SVG), replace media file without branding (replaces Enable Media Replace).
- Phase 5: Media 2, watermarking and WebP or AVIF images #17
  - Watermark pictures (replaces Easy Watermark): #17, Plugin Check fixes in #18.
  - WebP and AVIF with multisite support (replaces CompressX): #16.
- Phase 6: Links, short links with Pretty Links import and short CPT addresses #21
  - Short links: a `short-link` post type with slug, target, 301/302/307, nofollow, sponsored, click counts and categories, migrated from Pretty Links' `prli_links`: #21.
  - Remove CPT base: #19, with #20.
- Phase 7: Spectra, Kadence-compatible block replacements and Term list block #30
- Phase 8: Plugin presets with Apply, Reset and Undo #75
  - First batch for recommended plugins in #96. Follow-ups #100 to #105 are closed.
- Phase 9: wp-admin speed, load plugins only where needed #22
  - Learning admin screens and choosing plugins automatically: #267 (#164). Further speed work continues in #65.

## Decisions to report in the PRs

- **Index WP MySQL For Speed:** check whether its keys are present and whether they help at these sites' table sizes before deciding to reimplement, keep or drop it.
  - Decided: keep recommending it; Database keys protects its keys (`class-seoprostack-database-keys.php`).
- **String Locator:** remove it from the recommendations.
  - Done in #9.

## Verification per PR

- `php -l` and `node --check`
- Sync to LocalWP and run the existing browser audits plus a feature-specific check
- Plugin Check on a `.distignore` build
- WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 smoke test when core APIs are touched

title: feat: Hosting needs: OPcache and PHP memory advice from measured numbers
body:
## What

Plugin sizes shows how much PHP, JavaScript, CSS and media the installed and active plugins have, but not what that means for hosting. Sizing hosting against a site's load has always been hard to judge. Add a **Hosting needs** feature that turns measured numbers into plain advice and settings to ask the host for:

- **OPcache**: memory, file slots and interned strings, compared with how full OPcache is (`opcache_get_status()`) and with the PHP code that can load (core, theme, must-use plugins, drop-ins and active plugins). If the host keeps the status private (`opcache.restrict_api`), compare with the code size only.
- **PHP memory**: the highest peak per kind of request (pages, admin, REST API and cron) over 7 days, recorded at shutdown, compared with the limit that request ran under.
- **Memory per PHP worker**: the highest peak plus PHP's own overhead, with OPcache shared by all workers. The number of workers depends on uncached traffic, so the feature explains it rather than guessing.

## Where

- A row below the plugin list (after the Size totals), filled in by AJAX so the screen opens straight away.
- Two Site Health tests (OPcache size, PHP memory).
- A Hosting needs section on the Site Health Info tab, which is included when site info is copied for a host.

## Files

- New `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`, registered in `includes/class-seoprostack.php`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-sizes.php`: count PHP files per plugin, plus a public `php_code()` helper that shares the cache.
- `uninstall.php`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `php -l` on all changed files.
- Throwaway Docker sites: latest WordPress on PHP 8.3 with WooCommerce, and WordPress 6.2 on PHP 7.4. Test the default OPcache, a too-small OPcache, a restricted OPcache status and seeded high memory peaks. Check the row at 1440 and 375 px, the Site Health tests, the Info section and the copy text, and confirm debug.log stays empty.

title: feat: install, activate, deactivate and uninstall recommended plugins in place, with bulk setup
body:
## What

Free Plugins tab: manage recommended plugins without leaving the page, and set up a new site with many of them at once.

1. Cards: Install, Activate, Deactivate and Uninstall all happen in place (no trip to the Plugins screen).
   - Not installed: **Install Now**
   - Installed, inactive: **Activate** and **Uninstall**
   - Active: **Deactivate**
2. A new **All** view: every recommended plugin in a compact list grouped by type, with a checkbox per plugin and per group, Select all, and bulk actions (Install and activate, Install, Activate, Deactivate, Uninstall) that run one plugin at a time with per-row progress.

## Why

Activating from a card currently goes to Plugins → Installed, so setting up many plugins means many round trips. New sites need a quick way to add a set.

## How

- `admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php`: state buttons rendered by one PHP method, reused for cards, list rows and AJAX responses; new AJAX endpoint for activate/deactivate/state that only accepts slugs from `admin/data/free-plugins.php`, with `activate_plugin`/`deactivate_plugin` capability checks and the plugin's nonce. Install and delete use core `wp.updates.installPlugin` / `wp.updates.deletePlugin` (core `install-plugin` / `delete-plugin` AJAX, WordPress 4.6+), so filesystem credentials work as in core. No reliance on WordPress 6.5's `activate-plugin` AJAX (minimum is 6.2).
- `admin/includes/class-free-plugins-manager.php`: All link and list view markup.
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin.js`, `admin/css/seoprostack-admin.css`: controller and styles.
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`: feature notes and changelog.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `node --check`.
- Local test site: install, activate, deactivate, uninstall from cards; bulk install and activate a group from All; check `wp-content/debug.log`.
- WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 smoke test of the activate/deactivate endpoint.

title: feat: updates from GitHub through Git Updater
body:
## What

Let sites get SEO Pro Stack updates from GitHub releases through Git Updater, before (and alongside) WordPress.org.

## Why

The plugin is not on WordPress.org yet, and GitHub releases can go out as often as needed, so GitHub works as the early update channel. Git Updater is not on WordPress.org, so it has to be installed from GitHub.

## How

- `seoprostack.php`: `GitHub Plugin URI`, `Primary Branch: main`, `Release Asset: true` header lines. No `Update URI` header.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-github-updates.php` (new, optional): install/activate notice for Git Updater (nonce- and capability-checked admin-post actions, network-wide on multisite, PHP 8.0 check), Dismiss, Free Plugins card, and an off-by-default "Early updates from GitHub" setting (Maintenance tab) that adds the plugin to Git Updater's `gu_override_dot_org` filter.
- `includes/class-seoprostack.php`: `SEOProStack::$optional_features`, loaded only when the file is present, so the WordPress.org build can leave the file out.
- `admin/includes/class-plugin-manager.php`, `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: `seoprostack_free_plugins` and `seoprostack_external_plugins` filters; cards for plugins not on WordPress.org.
- `uninstall.php`, `README.md`, `readme.txt`, `AGENTS.md`: cleanup, docs, release rules.

## Acceptance

- GitHub build: notice on Dashboard, Plugins, Updates and SEO Pro Stack screens; one click installs and activates Git Updater's latest release.
- Build without the feature file loads with no Git Updater references in the UI.
- Plugin Check clean; PHP 7.4 / WordPress 6.2 compatible.

## Note

Git Updater reads the repository anonymously, so updates reach sites only once the repository is public. It stays private for now, by the owner's decision.

title: feat: release build, preflight and Plugin Check scripts; WordPress.org preflight plan
body:
## What

Release tooling and a WordPress.org preflight plan, ready for when the plugin goes public. No release, no submission.

- `scripts/build-release.sh`: build both zips from a Git ref with `.distignore` applied — the GitHub release zip (`seoprostack-X.Y.Z.zip`) and the WordPress.org zip without the GitHub updater file, named so Git Updater can never pick it.
- `scripts/preflight-release.sh`: static release checks (versions agree, no pre-release `Version:`, readme/header fields agree, no `Update URI`, PHP/JS syntax, zip layout, WordPress.org build free of updater code, remote assets, size), with errors vs warnings.
- `scripts/plugin-check.sh`: Plugin Check on built zips in a disposable Docker WordPress.
- `RELEASING.md`: the GitHub release steps and the WordPress.org preflight checklist, including the manual steps (slug, SVN, assets).

## Why

GitHub releases are built by hand today, and a WordPress.org zip attached to a GitHub release would be installed by Git Updater (it takes the first asset whose name starts with the slug). Submission has steps that are easy to miss, such as the slug coming from the plugin name.

## Acceptance

- Both zips build from `HEAD`, each with one `seoprostack/` folder; only the GitHub zip has `includes/features/class-seoprostack-github-updates.php`.
- Preflight passes on `main` apart from known warnings; it fails on a pre-release version or an `Update URI` header.
- Plugin Check runs on both zips and reports no errors.
- Scripts and `RELEASING.md` are left out of release builds.

title: feat: speed and hosting right-sizing roadmap
body:
## Aim

SEO Pro Stack should cover a site's speed needs and right-size its hosting: which plan to buy, how to allocate resources (PHP workers, RAM, CPU, OPcache, database), and which settings to use, with headroom for bursts of traffic. Everything stays off by default, measured rather than guessed, and reversible.

## Inspiration (ideas only, no code copied)

- **Super Speedy Performance Analysis** (GPL-3.0): token-gated profiling, per-plugin SQL/HTTP/memory attribution, autoload coverage, `information_schema` table sizes, `performance_schema` digests. Thresholds: autoload 1 MB, slow query 50 ms, big result 200 rows, persistent object cache advised above 500,000 postmeta rows or 10,000 products, PHP below 8.0 flagged.
- **Scalability Pro** (commercial): about 35 opt-in indexes built with `ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE`; `SQL_CALC_FOUND_ROWS` removal with look-ahead paging; deferred term counting with a nightly recount; an autoload optimiser with a logged, reversible change list; a "good settings" plan applied one step at a time with reasons for skipped items.
- **Code Profiler Pro** and **Super Speedy Imports**: per-plugin hook timing, by mapping each callback's file to its plugin.
- None of them sizes hosting. That is the gap SEO Pro Stack fills.

## Roadmap (ranked by value)

- [x] Hosting plans for low, medium and high traffic from this site's own numbers, measured traffic, and an OPcache need based on the code that can load (first child). Built: **Hosting needs** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`; README → Hosting to buy).
- [x] Autoload advisor: the largest autoloaded options, with options unused on key pages switched off through a logged, reversible change. Built: **Load large settings only where they are used** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-autoload-options.php`; learns which options of 10 KB or more page views read, stops autoloading the others, values unchanged).
- [x] Per-plugin cost on the Plugins screen: OPcache memory per plugin (from `opcache_get_status(true)`), with request time and queries on demand. Built: **Plugin sizes** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-sizes.php`) shows OPcache memory, and **Measure page time** (#447, PR #448, released in 1.1.0; `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-cost.php`) measures each plugin's page time, database queries, load time and memory, and calls to other sites on demand, through a token-gated must-use file that is removed afterwards (single sites).
- [x] Outbound HTTP audit in wp-admin: which plugin calls which host, how long it takes, and optional blocking (payment hosts never blocked). Built: **Calls to other sites** (#452, PR #453, released in 1.2.0; `includes/features/class-seoprostack-outbound-calls.php`): per plugin, theme or must-use plugin and host, counts, failures, total, average and slowest time, last answer, request kinds and last path without query strings; Block per plugin and host, with payment services, WordPress.org/.com, the site itself, WordPress, SEO Pro Stack and WordPress's update code never blocked.
- [x] Database index advisor: a small opt-in set, built online, removed on uninstall. Built: **Add database keys** (#455, PR #460, released in 1.2.0; `includes/features/class-seoprostack-added-keys.php`): `postmeta` and single-site `usermeta` `meta_key(191), meta_value(32)`, and Action Scheduler `status, scheduled_date_gmt`, each added with `ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE` only on request and never when an existing key covers it; only `sps_` keys are removed; WP-CLI `wp seoprostack keys`. The proposed posts `post_type, post_status, post_date` key is not offered: WordPress's own `type_status_date` key already covers it.
- [x] `SQL_CALC_FOUND_ROWS` removal for large archives, opt-in. Built: **Faster page counts on long lists** (#430, PR #438, released in 0.15.0; `includes/features/class-seoprostack-found-rows.php`), which keeps exact totals and page numbers instead of estimates.
- [x] Deferred term and comment counting with a scheduled recount, for imports and shops. Built: **Count terms and comments in the background** (#429, PR #441, released in 0.15.0; `includes/features/class-seoprostack-deferred-counts.php`).
- [x] Admin count caches (posts, users, WooCommerce dashboard). Built: **Remember admin counts** (#464, PR #467, released in 1.3.0; `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-counts.php`): without a persistent object cache, keeps the site's comment counts (as WooCommerce adjusts them), each post type's counts, `count_users()` and WooCommerce's pending product reviews count between requests in one non-autoloaded option, cleared on WordPress's change events and kept at most an hour. With 500,000 comments and WooCommerce, a settings screen's queries went from 189 ms to 12 ms. The WooCommerce dashboard status widget is already hidden by the default tidier admin (`admin/data/dashboard.php`).
- [x] A "recommended speed settings" plan that applies changes one at a time, explains each trade-off and can be reverted. Built: **Recommended speed settings** (#468, PR #471, released in 1.3.0; `includes/features/class-seoprostack-speed-plan.php`): below the Speed tab's settings, from the site's own size and plugins, which speed and server settings to turn on, why, the trade-off, and why others are not recommended here; one setting per click through the settings screen's own save path; Undo while the setting is still as the plan left it; changes logged in `seoprostack_speed_plan` (not autoloaded). Also fixed: settings saves ran out of memory on sites with tens of thousands of pages.

Each item got its own child issue (#429, #430, #447, #452, #455, #464, #468), all closed. New speed or hosting work gets a new issue.

title: feat: Hosting needs: plans for low, medium and high traffic from measured numbers
body:
## What

Hosting needs (#54) compares OPcache and PHP memory with this site's own use. Extend it into hosting plans to buy, using the plugins that are active and installed and the site's measured numbers:

- **Plans for low, medium and high traffic** (about 10,000, 100,000 and 1,000,000 visits a month): PHP workers, RAM, CPU cores, OPcache settings, PHP memory limit, object cache and the type of hosting. Assumptions are stated, including the busiest hour, bursts, the share of requests a page cache cannot serve (more for shops and member sites), and background requests.
- **Measured traffic**: sample 1 in 20 requests that reach PHP. Record time-per-request buckets (for the 95th percentile) per kind of request, and counts per hour. Then work out the workers this site needs now. Requests served by a page cache never reach PHP, so they are not counted.
- **OPcache need for all the code that can load**. The current suggestion is 1.5 times the use, which understates the need once OPcache is full: a Local test site suggested 192 MB and 16 MB, then used 186 MB and 31 MB within seconds of being raised. Use the measured ratio of compiled to source size (`opcache_get_status(true)`, 2.6 on that site; strings 0.7). Note that the interned strings buffer is part of `opcache.memory_consumption`. Also give the OPcache need if every installed plugin were active.
- **Advisories**: database size and autoloaded options (from one `information_schema` read and one sum query), persistent object cache (advised above 500,000 postmeta rows or 10,000 products, and for medium and high plans), page cache detected or not, and PHP version.

## Where

- The Plugins screen row gets a short summary and a compact plans table.
- The Site Health Info section gets a line per plan, so the details can be copied for a host.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`
- `uninstall.php` (new `seoprostack_hosting_traffic` option)
- `README.md`, `readme.txt`

## Verification

- Run `php -l`.

title: feat: move plugins' licence and update checks off page loads
body:
Part of #7 (see also the outbound HTTP audit in #65). The survey data and preview site are local to the owner, so this is worked in an interactive session.

## Aim

Licence and update checks that plugins make while a page or admin screen loads should run in the background instead, so they never delay a page. The owner approved this approach (option B) on 1 October 2026: inspect each call, move only calls shown to be safe, and keep updates and licences working.

## Evidence so far

A read-only survey of the owner's sites with HTTP Requests Manager logs (kept locally by the owner, not in the repository) found:

- page-load licence checks by premium plugins;
- repeated WordPress.org "not found" lookups for plugins that are not on WordPress.org;
- slow MainWP sync calls, self-site background queue calls, and Fluent Forms Pro → ActiveCampaign calls from cron (cron: leave alone unless it blocks a visitor's request).

## Constraints

- `AGENTS.md` → Code rules: do not change WordPress update behaviour (update transients, `auto_update_*`, update checks); Plugin Check reports `plugin_updater_detected`. This work must not filter core update transients. If a call can only be moved by touching updates, record it and leave it.
- Update `AGENTS.md` with the rule that results from the review (what may be deferred and how).
- Off by default; one feature class in `includes/features/`.

## Steps

1. For each host and plugin in the survey, read the calling code and classify it: needed on that request, safe to move to cron or a transient, or must stay.
2. Implement the moves for the safe group only (for example `pre_http_request` returning a cached answer and refreshing it in cron), each listed in `README.md`.
3. Then decide whether the test site still needs the "Disable All WordPress Updates" plugin, and recommend.

## Verification

Preview site with HTTP Requests Manager: requests per page load before and after; licence status screens still show the licence as active; Plugins and Updates screens still list updates.

body:
For #7. Follows PR #98 (starter data for FluentCRM and Fluent Boards).

## What

Add Fluent Forms to starter data: four example forms the owner uses on his own sites, each sending entries to the matching FluentCRM list through a FluentCRM feed. Same add-only, remove-while-unused rules as PR #98.

## Why

The owner wants new sites to start organised by example. His forms are named after their purpose, and each one feeds the FluentCRM list named after the form (`Website Contact Form` list ← Contact Form), so a contact's lists show where they came from.

## The pattern (read from the owner's main site, structure only)

| Form | Fields (element:label) | FluentCRM feed |
|---|---|---|
| Contact Form | input_name:names, input_email:Email, phone:Phone/Mobile, textarea:Your Message, gdpr_agreement:GDPR Agreement, input_checkbox:Subscribe | list `website-contact-form`; first/last/full name, phone, `source` = `{submission.source_url}` |
| Subscription Form | input_name:names, input_email:Email | list `website-newsletter-subscription-form`, tag `website-newsletter-subscriber`, double opt-in on, force subscribe |
| Discovery Call Form | input_name:names, input_text:Company, input_text:Role, input_email:Email, phone:Direct/Mobile Phone, input_url:Website, textarea:Your Message, textarea:Time Preferences, gdpr_agreement:GDPR Agreement, input_checkbox:Newsletter | list `website-booking-form`; company, role, website (the FluentCRM contact fields from PR #98), phone; tag router: Newsletter = "Subscribe to our newsletter" → `website-newsletter-subscriber` |
| GDPR Data Subject Access Request Form | section_break, input_radio:On behalf of, input_file:3rd-Party Authorisation Letter, input_checkbox:Data Subject Access Type(s), input_checkbox:Requests, input_name:names, input_date:Date of Birth, input_email:Email, phone:Phone/Mobile, address:Correspondence Address, input_file:Proof of Identity, input_file:Proof of Address, textarea:Notes, input_hidden: url, ip, http_referer, browser, os, gdpr_agreement:GDPR Agreement | list `data-subject-access-request-form`; address fields and phone; double opt-in on; tag router on Data Subject Access Type(s): Contractor → `contractor`, Customer → `customer-client`, Employee → `employee`, Supplier Contact → `supplier` |

The owner's FluentCRM feed mapped the Discovery Call Form to a "Clients"-type list on one site; use `website-booking-form` to keep "list = source". Notification emails: leave Fluent Forms' defaults (admin email) and never copy addresses from a live site.

## How

- `includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php`: add item type `fluentform_forms` (title, fields, crm_feed with list/tag slugs). Match by form title. Create through Fluent Forms' own code, not raw SQL: read `fluentform` source for how its form import (Tools → Import) builds a form from exported JSON (`form_fields`, `formSettings`, `notifications` meta) and reuse it. Add the FluentCRM feed as `fluentcrm_feeds` form meta with list/tag IDs resolved from slugs (reuse `map_path()` logic), only when FluentCRM is active. Remove: delete a recorded form only if it has no submissions (`fluentform_submissions` count 0), through Fluent Forms' own delete code.
- New `starters/fluentform.json` with the four forms and `notes` explaining the naming rule.
- Plugins screen and `wp seoprostack starters` already handle any starter file; check the Fluent Forms row shows it.

## Acceptance

- Submitting each form on the front end creates a FluentCRM contact in the named list with the mapped fields and tags.
- `remove` keeps a form that has an entry, removes the others.

## What

title: feat: presets clear plugins' object-cache groups; Code Snippets preset
body:
For #7. Follows PR #96.

## What

Let a preset name the object-cache groups to clear after it writes, then add a **Code Snippets** preset.

## Why

Code Snippets caches its settings in a versioned object-cache group. `SEOProStack_Presets` (`includes/class-seoprostack-presets.php`) only clears the option's own cache, so on sites with a persistent object cache (Redis, Memcached, LiteSpeed object cache) Code Snippets keeps the old settings after Apply, Reset or Undo. Found while choosing the PR #96 presets; check it again in the current Code Snippets source before relying on it.

## How

- Preset format: optional `"cache": {"groups": ["…"], "keys": {"group": ["key"]}}`. After `write()` and `undo()`, call `wp_cache_flush_group()` when available (WP 6.1+, guard with `function_exists()` and `wp_cache_supports('flush_group')`), else `wp_cache_delete()` for listed keys; if a plugin bumps a version key to invalidate, document and call its own function instead when it exists.
- Read Code Snippets' settings code for its cache group and invalidation, then `presets/code-snippets.json` (for example: no promotions or upsell notices, editor settings that do not load remote assets). Leave out settings whose save handler does more.
- Docs: format line in the class docblock, `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (≤ 10,240 bytes).

## Acceptance

With a persistent object cache in the test site (for example the Redis Object Cache plugin and a Redis container), Apply then reading the setting through Code Snippets' own getter returns the new value without a cache flush; same for Reset and Undo.

title: feat: list and remove leftover or redundant database keys, per site with confirmation
body:
For #7. Ref #65 (the "Database index advisor" item adds keys; this removes leftover ones).

## What

List redundant and leftover keys (indexes) on WordPress core tables, and remove the ones an admin picks on that site, after a confirmation. Off by default.

## Why

A read-only survey of the owner's sites (issue #7 comment on Index WP MySQL For Speed) found 7 sites still carrying keys added by plugins that are gone or replaced (`wpi_*`, `spro_*`, `wdbi_*`), and one site whose `posts` table has 15 keys, several covered by others, which slows every write. The owner chose: plan the cleanup, with confirmation per site (option 4B).

## How

- New feature class in `includes/features/` (Plugins or a Maintenance tab), off by default, `manage_options` + nonce on every action.
- Read keys from `information_schema.STATISTICS` for core tables (`posts`, `postmeta`, `options`, `usermeta`, `users`, `terms`, `term_taxonomy`, `term_relationships`, `termmeta`, `comments`, `commentmeta`, plus the multisite ones).
- Classify each non-core key: **leftover** (name prefix of a known plugin that is not active: `wpi_`, `spro_`, `wdbi_`, …), **redundant** (its columns are a left prefix of another key on the same table), or **in use by an active plugin** (for example Index WP MySQL For Speed's own keys while it is active: never offer these). Never offer core's own keys (compare with the schema in `wp-admin/includes/schema.php` for the running version) or primary keys.
- Show table, key, columns, why it is offered and the size. Removing runs `ALTER TABLE … DROP INDEX` per chosen key, logs what was dropped with a `CREATE INDEX` line to put it back, and shows that line to the admin.
- Nothing stored except the log option (remove it in `uninstall.php`).
- Docs: `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (≤ 10,240 bytes).

## Acceptance

On a throwaway site seeded with a duplicate key on `postmeta`, a `wpi_` key and Index WP MySQL For Speed's keys with that plugin active: the list offers the duplicate and the `wpi_` key, not core or active-plugin keys; removing one drops it and logs its `CREATE INDEX` line; running that line restores it.

## Verification

## Aim

1. Replace Git Updater with SEO Pro Stack's own GitHub release updater, so sites need one plugin less and PHP 7.4 sites get updates. It must work for any installed plugin that names its GitHub repository (the `GitHub Plugin URI` header Git Updater already reads), because more plugins will be released on GitHub.
2. On the Plugins screen, tell people which active plugins SEO Pro Stack replaces, so they can deactivate and delete them.

## Why

Git Updater needs PHP 8.0 (we support 7.4), bundles Freemius, and is a whole plugin for one job. WordPress core already downloads, installs, auto-updates and rolls back; it only needs to be told a release exists.

  - keep the headers so Git Updater keeps working until it is deactivated.
- Plugins screen notice for active plugins a setting replaces (deactivate link, or a link to switch the setting on) and installed inactive ones (delete link).

**WordPress (new switches, probably on the Speed or Admin tab)**

- `wp_rest_api_disable`: REST API for logged-out visitors only, with an allow list for routes the site's plugins use publicly (forms, WooCommerce Store API, oEmbed).

- `marketing_disable`: Marketing hub (`woocommerce_marketing_menu_items`, `woocommerce_admin_features`).

- `woo_merchant_email_notifications` (new in Disable Bloat 4.0): read what it does in its source first.

title: fix: fitted admin menu leaves a strip beside the open menu, changes width between loads and still wraps names
body:
Found on the preview site in "Organise the admin menu → Fit the menu to its names", added by PR #120 (merged as 5b6e3e9, on by default, not yet released). Verification needs the owner's preview site, so this is worked in an interactive session.

## What happens

On a page inside **Developers** (so the menu opens in place, with the page's list under its entry), the widened sidebar shows these problems (owner's screenshots, two loads of the same screen):

1. **A strip to the right of the open menu.** The open Developers list (Settings flyout and the entries below it, Anti-Malware … WP-Optimize) stays about 300 px wide, but the sidebar background is wider. The strip between them is dark on one load. On another load it takes the current entry's highlight colour (the blue of the selected "Developers" row), running the full height of the open list.
2. **The width differs between loads.** The sidebar is a few pixels wider in the second screenshot.
3. **Names in the open list still wrap**, although the sidebar was widened for them: "ACF: Better Search", "Cloudflare Turnstile", "Debug Log Manager", "HTTP Requests Manager", "Plugin Check (Tools)", "Scheduled Actions".
4. **A wrapped top-level name loses its indent.** "LiteSpeed Cache" puts "Cache" on a second line under the icon instead of under "LiteSpeed".

Expected: the open in-place list fills the sidebar's width with no strip or stray highlight, the width is the same on every load, and names fit on one line (up to the 280 px limit). Where a name must still wrap, the second line lines up with the first.

## Where to look

- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js` `fit()` measures once with `body.sps-menu-measure` and sets `--sps-menu-width` on `<body>`. `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css` applies it to `#adminmenuback`, `#adminmenuwrap` and `#adminmenu`. The rule for the current menu's in-place flyout (`.wp-has-current-submenu .wp-submenu li.current.sps-menu-has-sub > ul.sps-menu-flyout`) and the in-place `.wp-submenu` of the Administrators and Developers menus keep their own width, which likely causes the strip.
- Check whether the measurement includes the in-place open list (its entries have extra left padding) and whether `fit()` can run before or after the highlight styles load. That could explain the different widths and colours between loads.
- Hanging indent: top-level `.wp-menu-name` next to `.wp-menu-image` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php` output and the stylesheet.
- Fix it before the next release, because the feature is on by default. If it cannot be fixed in time, ask the owner whether to turn "Fit the menu to its names" off by default for that release.

## Verification

Preview site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`). Open a Developers page (such as Tools → Scheduled Actions) and an Administrators page, and reload each several times: same width, no strip, no wrapping up to 280 px. Also check a normal menu (Posts) and side flyouts, the collapsed sidebar, at 960 px and below, and the block editor. Screenshots at ≤1568 px, light admin colours and Modern. Debug log and browser console clean.

title: fix: Licence checks dialog returns after Ask me again
body:
## Problem

Ask before licence checks: clicking **Ask me again → tomorrow** does not stop the Licence checks dialog coming back. It alternates between Kadence Blocks and Starter Templates by Kadence WP (both `licensing.stellarwp.com`).

## Cause

`SEOProStack_Licence_Calls::handle()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-licence-calls.php`, `do=later`) wrote the `seoprostack_licence_later` user meta as one `until` plus `hidden` (ID => first held), **replacing** the previous value. When a second plugin started waiting after the first was hidden, the dialog showed only the second; hiding it overwrote the first plugin's hide, so the first came back, and so on.

Evidence from the shared test site: meta `hidden` held only `1c5c3a7d6500` (kadence-blocks) while `49a0079678cb` (kadence-starter-templates, first held later) was waiting.

## Fix

Each hidden check keeps its own `first` and `until`; new hides are merged with those still standing; the earlier shape (shared `until`) is still read. New helper `later_hidden()` used by `handle()` and `shown_entries()`.

## Verification

`php -l`; on the test site, hide the second plugin while the first is hidden and confirm both stay hidden (`shown_entries()` empty, meta lists both).

title: fix: dark plugin icons invisible in the Administrators and Developers menus
body:
## What

In Organise the admin menu, plugin icons inside the **Administrators** and **Developers** menus (open in place and as a flyout) are hard or impossible to see on the dark admin menu: Site Assist, ICS Calendar, FluentCRM, Bit Social and Bit Integrations are black or dark grey; AutomatorWP shows nothing on screens where Load plugins only where needed skips it.

## Why

- `icon_html()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php` prints a plugin's base64 SVG icon as a plain `background-image`. Core's `wp-admin/js/svg-painter.js` repaints SVG icons only for top-level `.wp-menu-image` elements, so these keep their own fill: none (black), `currentColor` (black in a background image) or grey.
- AutomatorWP's icon is its own icon-font class (`dashicons-automatorwp`), defined in its stylesheet, which is not loaded where the plugin is skipped.

## How

- `icon_html()`: base64 SVG data icons get `.sps-menu-icon-svg` and a `--sps-menu-icon` custom property; `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css` draws them as a mask over `currentColor`, so they follow the text, hover and current colours (as core paints top-level icons). Other images (GIF, SVG files by URL) keep their own colours, as in core.
- `:where(#adminmenu .sps-menu-icon.dashicons-before)::before { content: "\f111" }`: core's cog when an icon class has no stylesheet; zero specificity so any loaded icon class wins.

## Verify

- `php -l includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-menu.php`
- Admin menu on the shared test site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`), dark scheme: Administrators menu open and as a flyout; Site Assist, ICS Calendar, FluentCRM, Bit Social and Bit Integrations visible; hover changes their colour; AutomatorWP shows its icon on the Plugins screen and a cog where skipped.

title: Plugins' fixed bars sit under the fitted (wider) admin menu
body:
## Problem

With **Organise the admin menu → Fit the menu to its names** on, the sidebar can be wider than WordPress's usual 160px. Many plugins place their own fixed headers, footers, notices and panels for the 160px menu, so the wider menu covers their start or pushes their end off screen. Example: Fluent Support's setup footer (`.fs_setup .fs_sticky_footer { position: fixed; left: 160px; right: 0 }`) shows "ed Help?" with its start under the menu.

Patterns found in plugins installed on the test site:

- `left: 160px` (Fluent Support, Kadence, WP-Optimize, Tutor LMS, SliceWP, WP Social Reviews, Admin Columns, Freemius notices)
- `margin-left: 160px` on a `left: 0; right: 0` bar (Kadence Starter Templates)
- `padding-left: 160px` on a full-window fixed element (Freemius `.fs-modal`)
- `width: calc(100% - 160px)` (React Query devtools, WooCommerce-style headers)

## Approach

Universal, not per plugin: `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js` checks elements fixed to the window (and absolute ones positioned on `<body>`) as they appear and when their class or style changes. One that starts under the wider menu (160px up to the fitted width, not centred) gets `sps-fit-start` / `sps-fit-margin`; a full-window one with 160px+ padding gets `sps-fit-pad`; one now running off the far side gets `sps-fit-width`. Offsets of their own are kept in `--sps-fit-*` custom properties. `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css` applies these only at 961px+ with the menu expanded, so collapsing the menu or a narrow window restores the plugin's own layout. Elements a script places inline (dropdowns, popovers) and the admin menu and toolbar are skipped.

## Verification

- `node --check admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`
- Shared test site: Fluent Support setup footer starts at the menu's edge; Kadence/WP-Optimize headers line up; collapsing the menu restores 36px layouts; no console errors; debug log clean.

title: Fitted admin menu width differs between screens (203–217px)
body:
## Problem

**Organise the admin menu → Fit the menu to its names** promises the same menu width on every screen (`README.md` → "Every menu and folded section counts, so the width is the same on every screen"). On the shared test site (Chrome, 1440×900) the fitted width varies:

| Screen | `--sps-menu-width` | Widest entry (measured need) | Entries measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edit.php` | 207px | HTTP Requests Manager (third level, 205) | 380 |
| `admin.php?page=fluent-support` | 207px | HTTP Requests Manager (205) | 380 |
| `admin.php?page=WP-Optimize` | 203px | HTTP Requests Manager (201, in the open menu) | 380 |
| `admin.php?page=tutor_settings` | 210px | HTTP Requests Manager (207) | 379 |
| `post-new.php` | 217px | "Try BBForms!New" (third level, 215) | 383 |

So the menu moves sideways by up to 14px between screens.

## Two causes

1. **The same entry measures differently on different screens.** "HTTP Requests Manager" (a third-level Developers entry) needs 201, 205 or 207px depending on the screen. `room()` in `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js` uses `IN_PLACE_INDENT` (38) for third-level entries, then adds the text width measured from the content box and the link's `padding-right`. That padding (and maybe the text box) differs between a flyout list, a list shown in place under the current entry (`li.current.sps-menu-has-sub`, see `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css`), and an entry in the open menu (WP-Optimize, 201). The in-place width should be worked out from fixed numbers (indent + text width + the in-place padding-right), not from wherever the entry happens to be when measured.
2. **Some entries only exist on some screens.** `post-new.php` has 383 entries, including a BBForms promotion ("Try BBForms!" plus a "New" badge), and `tutor_settings` has 379. Plugins add or remove menu entries per screen, possibly also because of Load plugins only where needed. Options: leave badge text (`.update-plugins`, `.awaiting-mod`, "New" spans) out of the measurement and/or remember the widest width per user (for example `setUserSetting`, as the folding does) so it stays the same across screens.

## Files

- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`: `room()`, `fit()`, `IN_PLACE_INDENT`, `FIT_MIN` / `FIT_MAX`
- `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css`: third-level in-place padding, `sps-menu-measure` rules
- Docs if the behaviour changes: `README.md` (Fit the menu to its names), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (stay under 10 KB)

### Files Scope

- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`
- `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`
- `readme.txt`

## Verification

On the shared test site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`), read `getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--sps-menu-width')` on `edit.php`, `post-new.php`, `admin.php?page=WP-Optimize`, `admin.php?page=tutor_settings` and `admin.php?page=fluent-support`. All five should match. No entry should wrap onto two lines on any of them. Run `node --check admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`. Plugins' bars that follow the menu (#144) should still line up.

title: feat: block editor opens faster (measure, then fix the biggest costs)
body:
Part of #7. Follows #91 (PR #160).

## Aim

The block editor (Posts/Pages → Add New, and editing a post) should open as fast as it can. Find where the time goes when it opens, then make the changes that save the most, as SEO Pro Stack features or additions to existing ones. Each change needs measured before and after numbers.

## What we know

On the shared preview site (WordPress 7.1.2, Kadence theme, 80 active plugins, `SCRIPT_DEBUG` and `WP_DEBUG` on), from #91's measurements with headless Chromium:

- `post-new.php?post_type=page` took 6.5–12 s until Kadence's toolbar button was ready, with Faster editor with Kadence Blocks already on. That feature brought the page from about 24 MB to about 8.7 MB.
- A CPU profile of opening the design library showed React development builds (`react-jsx-runtime.js`, `jsxDEV`), because `SCRIPT_DEBUG` is on. Measure with `SCRIPT_DEBUG` off as well, since live sites run production builds. Otherwise the numbers mislead.
- Measure with the shipped settings, then with each candidate change alone.

Features that already touch the editor: Load plugins only where needed (`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`, `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`), Tidy editor (`class-seoprostack-editor-tidy.php`), Faster editor with Kadence Blocks (`class-seoprostack-kadence-library.php`), Fewer Heartbeat requests (`class-seoprostack-heartbeat.php`) and Licence checks (`class-seoprostack-licence-calls.php`).

## Steps

1. Measure the server time for `post-new.php` and `post.php` (Query Monitor or `SAVEQUERIES`, timing per plugin), and in the browser record total transfer, script count and size, REST requests the editor makes on load (`wp.apiFetch` calls, preloaded paths), long tasks, and time until the editor accepts typing. Record a baseline with `SCRIPT_DEBUG` on and off.
2. List what is loaded and what each costs: plugins' `enqueue_block_editor_assets` / `enqueue_block_assets` scripts and styles (including in the editor canvas iframe), inline data (`wp_add_inline_script` / `wp_localize_script` payloads), REST calls on load that could be preloaded (`block_editor_rest_api_preload_paths`) or deferred, block registrations, patterns from remote sources (`should_load_remote_block_patterns`, `wp/v2/block-patterns/patterns`), meta boxes that force the compatibility layout, and Heartbeat or autosave work at load.
3. Rank candidates by saved time. Implement the clear wins that are safe and generic, following the pattern of the Kadence fix. Where a fix belongs to one plugin, it uses that plugin's own filters where it has them.
4. Anything that changes what loads for a plugin must keep that plugin working in the editor. Open the editor with it, insert its blocks and save a post, and check the debug log for new messages mentioning `seoprostack` or a plugin it affects.

## Constraints

- Features are off by default unless the owner says otherwise; each new setting goes through `settings()` (see `AGENTS.md`).
- PHP 7.4 / WordPress 6.2 APIs; guard newer ones with `function_exists()`.
- Do not change WordPress update behaviour.
- #93 (Customizer, Site Health, Import and Export load only the plugins they need) is in progress in the same plugin-loader files. If a change here touches `class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` or `class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`, start from `main` after #93 merges.

## Files

Found during step 2; likely `includes/features/class-seoprostack-editor-tidy.php` or a new class in `includes/features/`, registered in `SEOProStack::$core_features` (`includes/class-seoprostack.php`), and docs in `README.md`, `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (stay under 10 KB).

## Verification

- A before/after table in the PR for each change, with the conditions stated (`SCRIPT_DEBUG`, cold or warm cache, logged-in admin, same browser). For noisy timings, alternate with and without the change in one session and report medians (as in PR #160's second comment).
- `php -l` on PHP 7.4 and 8.x, `node --check`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` with 0 errors.
- Editor still loads, inserts and saves posts with the affected plugins; no new debug log messages.

title: feat: Load plugins only where needed learns in the background and chooses plugins itself
body:
Part of #7. Follows #93 (PR #163).

## Aim

Load plugins only where needed should work without people having to understand it. SEO Pro Stack makes the decisions; settings stay only as ways to bypass something that causes a problem.

1. **Background learning.** Screens are fast from the first visit, including after plugin updates. Today everything learned is forgotten on each update, activation or deactivation, so every screen is slow once again until an administrator opens it. With automatic updates that can happen daily.
2. **Plugins are chosen automatically.** Today people tick the plugins that should load only where needed, which means knowing which plugins are safe to skip. SEO Pro Stack should choose, and the list becomes a bypass: "Always load these plugins".

The owner's direction: "better if we can make decisions for the user, and options are just there to bypass things in case they are causing issues."

## Current behaviour (read first)

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `boot()` hooks `upgrader_process_complete` → `forget()` (line ~225); `forget()` deletes `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::MAP` (`seoprostack_plugin_map`), `MENU` and the front-end options (~434); `learn()` saves what a fully loaded request showed (~868); `sensitive_plugins()` finds plugins that must always load (login, active-plugin and permission changes).
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `MAP`, `MAP_VERSION` (6), `LIST_KEY` (`plugin_loading_only`, the ticked list), `fingerprint()` of active plugins (a change makes the map stale), `state()`.
- `README.md` → "Load plugins only where needed (Plugins)" documents every rule; keep it accurate.

## Part 1: background learning

- When the map is forgotten or goes stale, keep a short list of the admin screens it had learned (their URLs as an administrator opened them: GET, no `action`, nonce or other state-changing arguments). Keep the list most-used first, capped at about 30 entries, in an option that `uninstall.php` removes.
- On the next admin page an administrator (`activate_plugins`) opens, a small script fetches those screens one at a time with the administrator's own session (`fetch(url, { credentials: 'same-origin' })`), only when the browser is idle (`requestIdleCallback` with a timeout fallback). Each fetch learns that screen as an ordinary visit would.
  - Only one tab at a time: use a short-lived lock (`localStorage` or an option with an expiry).
  - Stop when the list is done or the page is left. Wait between requests so the administrator's own clicks are not queued behind them.
  - Never fetch a screen that is not on the list, and never anything that saves or changes state.
- No server-side loopback with forwarded or created login cookies, and no cron learning as a user.
- Screens that always load every plugin (see README) are skipped.
- Visitors' pages are never affected.

## Part 2: decide for the user

- Every active plugin loads only where needed, except:
  - plugins `sensitive_plugins()` reports (login, permissions, active-plugin filters);
  - network-activated plugins and other cases README already says always load;
  - plugins on a new bypass list, "Always load these plugins" (admin), which is empty by default.
- Existing sites keep what they chose. Migrate in `migrate()` / `maybe_migrate()` (bump `SEOProStack_Settings::DB_VERSION`, add a line to the `maybe_migrate()` docblock): if `plugin_loading_only` was saved, its unticked plugins go into the bypass list, so nothing changes for them. With no saved list, the bypass list starts empty.
- The settings panel shows the switch, then the bypass list with one plain sentence: when to add a plugin (a box, field or menu entry is missing on a screen, or something breaks), and that the admin bar reload links fix one-off cases.
- Do not change the front-end options ("Plugins to skip on the site", page learning) in this issue: skipping plugins for visitors carries more risk. Note anything there that could also be decided automatically in the PR, as a follow-up.
- Do not turn the feature on by default; that needs the owner's say (`AGENTS.md`).

## Constraints

- PHP 7.4 / WordPress 6.2 APIs; capability and nonce checks; admin copy short and plain.
- #162 (block editor speed) is running at the same time and may touch the same files. Merge `origin/main` into this branch before opening the PR, and again before merge.
- Update `README.md` (feature section, changelog), `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (under 10 KB).

## Verification

- On a throwaway WordPress site with 20 or more plugins (some with their own admin screens, meta boxes, list columns, a security or role plugin):
  - Part 1: visit a few screens, update or deactivate/reactivate a plugin, open one admin page, wait, then open the other screens. They load with fewer plugins on the first visit (admin bar Plugins menu count), and the background requests show one at a time in the browser's network log.
  - Part 2: a fresh settings save with nothing ticked filters every plugin except sensitive ones. A site with a saved tick list keeps the same plugins loading on the same screens after migration (compare the admin bar counts before and after).
  - The bypass list keeps a plugin loading everywhere.
- No new debug log messages mentioning `seoprostack`; `php -l` on PHP 7.4 and 8.x, `node --check`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` with 0 errors.

body:
For #7.

## What

Tidy the Free Plugins list (`admin/data/free-plugins.php`):

- Remove **Disable All WordPress Updates** (`disable-wordpress-updates`). title: feat: Short links replaces Lasso Lite (Simple URLs) and imports its links
body:
## What

Short links (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-short-links.php`) also replaces **Lasso Lite (Simple URLs)** (`simple-urls`), the way it already replaces Pretty Links: it imports Lasso Lite's links, groups and click counts, so a site can deactivate and delete Lasso Lite and keep every `/go/…` address working.

## Why

The owner asked for SEO Pro Stack's own short links to take over from Lasso Lite. We cannot make Lasso Lite itself use our feature, but we can replace it. Lasso Lite 159 is heavy for what most sites use it for (cloaked redirects). It loads a bundled Guzzle, three custom tables and promotions, and it contacts lasso.link from wp-admin. The worst of those calls is worked around by Fixes for other plugins (PR #177, GH#162); the others remain. AGENTS.md: "Decide for the user" and "Site owner in control, performance first".

## Facts from Lasso Lite 159's code (`wp-content/plugins/simple-urls/`)

- Links are posts of type `surl` (`SIMPLE_URLS_SLUG`, `Constant::LASSO_POST_TYPE` in `admin/constant.php`). The address is `/{rewrite slug}/{post_name}/`. The rewrite slug is `go` unless the `simple_urls_slug` filter changes it (`includes/class-simple-urls.php`, `get_cloak_rewrite_slug()`).
- Post meta (`classes/class-meta-enum.php`): `_surl_redirect` (target URL), `_surl_count` (clicks), `_enable_nofollow`, `_enable_sponsored`, `_open_new_tab`. The rest (`_price`, `_badge_text`, `_buy_btn_text`, thumbnails, `_show_disclosure`) are for Lasso's product displays, not redirects.
- Groups: taxonomy `lasso-lite-cat` (`Constant::LASSO_CATEGORY`).
- Settings: option `lassolite_settings` (`classes/class-setting.php`, defaults in `Constant::DEFAULT_SETTINGS`). Check it for a redirect type and nofollow/sponsored defaults to import.
- Custom tables `wp_lasso_lite_url_details`, `wp_lasso_lite_amazon_products`, `wp_lasso_lite_revert`: read them only if they hold redirect data that the post meta lacks. Confirm this from the code.
- Lasso Lite also shows product boxes (`[lasso …]` shortcode, a block and an Elementor widget). Short links does not replace those. The Plugins screen line must name that job, as it does for Disable Bloat's REST API switches (`admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php`), so nobody deletes Lasso Lite while posts still use its displays.

## How (follow the Pretty Links pattern in the same file)

1. `settings()`: add `'simple-urls' => 'Lasso Lite (Simple URLs)'` to `'replaces'` next to `'pretty-link'`.
2. Link import: extend the existing importer (`IMPORT` admin-post action, `IMPORT_BUDGET`, `handle_import()`, `cli_import()` behind `wp seoprostack short-links import`, and the "still to be imported" handling in `add_presets()`) with a Lasso Lite source. Map `post_name` to the slug under the same prefix, `_surl_redirect` to the target, `_surl_count` to the click count, and nofollow/sponsored to the link's own settings. Map `lasso-lite-cat` terms to `sps_short_link_cat`. Skip slugs already taken (`slug_owner()`) and report them. Run it again safely without duplicates.
3. `migrate()`: import Lasso Lite's relevant `lassolite_settings` with `self::import_setting()` (fills only unset keys). Bump `SEOProStack_Settings::DB_VERSION` (main is at 8 after #176) and add a line to the `maybe_migrate()` docblock. Never write or delete Lasso Lite's options or posts.
4. `admin/data/free-plugins.php`: remove `'simple-urls'` (line 53) with a comment, as earlier replaced plugins were removed.
5. Docs in the same PR: `README.md` (Short links section, Features table row for replaced plugins, Credits row: plugin, maker, WordPress.org page and the maker's own source repository, each checked with the WordPress.org plugin API or `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}`; if the maker has no public repository, say so rather than linking a mirror), `changelog.txt`, and `readme.txt` (stays under 10 KB). Anything new that is stored must be removed in `uninstall.php`.
6. Keep `presets/simple-urls.json` for sites that keep Lasso Lite.

## Acceptance

- On a throwaway site with Lasso Lite 159 and about 5 links (different targets, one with nofollow, one sponsored, two groups, click counts above 0, one slug clashing with an existing short link), importing creates matching short links. Each `/go/{slug}/` gives the same redirect target before and after Lasso Lite is deactivated. Counts and groups carry over, and the clash is reported and skipped.
- Running the import a second time adds nothing.
- The Plugins screen suggests deactivating Lasso Lite and names its product displays as something SEO Pro Stack does not replace.
- Pretty Links import still works unchanged.
- No new PHP errors, warnings, notices or deprecations mentioning `seoprostack` in the debug log. PHP 7.4 / WordPress 6.2 smoke test (Docker `wordpress:php7.4-apache`).

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-short-links.php`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php`
- EDIT: `admin/includes/class-replaced-plugins.php`
- EDIT: `admin/data/free-plugins.php`
- EDIT: `uninstall.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`

## Verification

`php -l` on changed files; `scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline` with 0 errors; `wp seoprostack short-links import` on the throwaway site; `curl -sI https://<site>/go/<slug>/` for each link before and after deactivating Lasso Lite; `scripts/preview-site.sh` after opening the PR. The shared preview has Lasso Lite active but no links, so seed links only on your own throwaway site, never the shared one.

title: fix: empty strip beside the full screen block editor with the fitted admin menu
body:
## Problem

With "Fit the menu to its names" on, the block editor in full screen mode (admin menu hidden) leaves an empty strip down the left side as wide as the fitted menu. The editor starts where the wider menu would end.

Seen on WordPress 7.1 (full screen mode keeps the admin bar).

## Cause (to confirm)

`admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css` and `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js` offset content for the fitted menu whenever the menu is not collapsed (`body.sps-menu-fit:not(.folded)`). In full screen mode core hides `#adminmenumain` (`body.js.is-fullscreen-mode`), but:

- `#wpcontent` / `#wpfooter` keep `margin-inline-start: var(--sps-menu-width)`; core's `margin-left: 0` has the same specificity.
- The watcher (`wide()`) still treats the menu as showing, so fixed bars marked `sps-fit-*` keep their `!important` offset.

## Fix

Treat full screen mode like a hidden menu: exclude `.is-fullscreen-mode` in the stylesheet's fitted-menu rules and in `wide()`.

## Files

- `admin/css/seoprostack-admin-menu.css`
- `admin/js/seoprostack-admin-menu.js`
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` (changelog line)

## Verification

Throwaway site, fitted menu wider than 160px: open the block editor, toggle full screen on and off; no strip in full screen, editor beside the menu otherwise. `node --check` the script.

title: fix: More menu items shift right under a taller icon
body:
## What

In the admin bar's More menu (…), some items are pushed to the right: Rank Math SEO under AutomatorWP, and Query Monitor under Social Posts.

## Why

Core floats bar icons (`.ab-icon`, `.ab-item:before`) left, and plugins do the same. On the bar every item is one line, so the floats never matter. In the menu a row (`min-height: 26px`) can be shorter than its icon, so the float spills into the next row and pushes its content right by the icon's width.

Measured on the shared test site (Chromium, `/wp-admin/edit.php`): Query Monitor's text started 36px into its row instead of 10px.

## How

Contain floats per row, for any plugin, with no per-plugin rules: a clearfix on each moved item's `.ab-item` in `SEOProStack_Admin_Bar_More::assets()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-bar-more.php`). It works for block rows and flex rows (TranslatePress). No plugin on the test site styles `.ab-item::after`.

## Verify

- Open … in the admin bar with Rank Math SEO, AutomatorWP, Social Posts and Query Monitor active: every row's icon and text start at the left padding.

title: fix: page learning stops Plugins to skip on the site; learning during Health Check troubleshooting
body:
Part of #7. Found while mapping Freesoul Deactivate Plugins against SEO Pro Stack in #92.

## Problems

### 1. Page learning switches off the site-wide list for many requests

With **Learn which plugins each page needs** on, **Plugins to skip on the site** stops applying to:

- any request with a cookie or an authentication header: returning visitors with a consent or analytics cookie, and logged-in people even when **Also skip them for people who are logged in** is on (`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php:547-550`, again at `:584-586`);
- any address with a query argument, because `front_page_key()` returns `''` (`:587-590`): searches, page numbers, campaign tags.

`start_front()` returns before `$chosen` (the ticked list) reaches `front_skipped()`, so nothing is skipped. With page learning off, the same requests skip the ticked plugins (README → Load plugins only where needed → "Only plain page views"). An extra opt-in should only add skipping, never remove it. Introduced in d0d03b2 (PR #151).

### 2. Learning while Health Check is troubleshooting

Health Check & Troubleshooting's troubleshooting mode loads fewer plugins for one person (its MU plugin filters `option_active_plugins` while the `wp-health-check-disable-plugins` cookie is set). SEO Pro Stack does not notice, so a screen or the site learned in that state records what the reduced set needed, under the fingerprint of the full active list (`fingerprint(stored_active_plugins())`). Later requests then skip plugins that screen needs. Freesoul Deactivate Plugins stands aside in that mode (`mu-plugins/eos-deactivate-plugins.php:3076-3081`, FDP 2.6.9).

## Fix

1. In `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::start_front()`, use page learning only when the request qualifies (no cookies or authentication, not logged in, non-empty `front_page_key()`). Otherwise fall through to the site-wide list exactly as with page learning off, including the logged-in choice. Keep the learning guards in `learn_front()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php:1056-1064`) as they are, so pages are still only learned from cookie-free public requests.
2. When the `wp-health-check-disable-plugins` cookie is present, load every plugin and learn nothing, in wp-admin and on the site. Check the cookie directly: it needs no Health Check code and does not depend on MU plugin load order.
3. Update `README.md` (Load plugins only where needed: page learning adds to the site-wide list; troubleshooting mode loads every plugin), `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (stay under 10 KB).

## Verification

On a throwaway WordPress site (AGENTS.md → Testing, step 2 "To check your branch on its own" and step 4), never the shared preview site:

- Add a one-file test plugin that prints `<!-- sps-marker -->` in `wp_footer`, tick it under Plugins to skip on the site, let the site learn.
- Page learning on: `curl` the home page with a cookie (`-b 'cmplz_banner-status=dismissed'`), with `?s=test`, with `?utm_source=x`, and logged in with "Also skip them for people who are logged in" on: the marker is absent in all four. Before the fix it is present.
- Page learning off: same results as before the fix.
- Health Check: start troubleshooting mode, open a few admin screens and a page of the site; `wp option get seoprostack_plugin_map` and `seoprostack_plugin_front` do not change; after leaving troubleshooting mode, screens show their plugins' boxes and menu entries.
- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh`, no new `debug.log` lines mentioning `seoprostack`.

### Files Scope

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`
- `readme.txt`

No notes means: no shortcodes, blocks, widgets or public content types, no page hooks, no login, email or admin bar hooks, not needed by a plugin that loads.

On the first learn after the update, on a site that had saved a ticked list, add the plugins that would now be skipped automatically but were not ticked to the bypass list, once (record that it ran). title: feat: page learning decides by post type and content, on the first visit, without expiry
body:
Part of #7. From the Freesoul Deactivate Plugins comparison in #92. Start after #223 and #164 merge (same files).

## Why

Freesoul Deactivate Plugins' most used rule is per post type: on 5 of the 12 surveyed sites with FDP active, 40 to 84 plugins are switched off across 9 to 18 post types (WooCommerce, Fluent Forms, Fluent Booking, Fluent Support, FluentCRM, Tutor LMS, Complianz Terms and admin tools on post types that do not use them), with per-post settings as exceptions. FDP decides before plugins load, from the address and one lookup by path, on every visit including the first, and the decision never expires.

SEO Pro Stack's **Learn which plugins each page needs** (#90, PR #151) learns per address instead:

- at most 100 hashed addresses (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::PAGE_LIMIT`), each for one hour (`includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php:592`);
- the first visit to an address, and the first after an hour, loads every plugin and rewrites the autoloaded `seoprostack_plugin_front` option during a visitor's request (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::learn_front()`).

With a page cache, the requests that reach PHP are mostly those first visits, so few of them skip anything, and on sites with hundreds of posts most addresses are never known.

## Aim

Decide for any public page before plugins load, from what is known without loading them, and keep the decision until content, settings, theme or plugins change (`seoprostack_plugin_front_revision` and the active-plugins fingerprint already track those).

- **Learn per page kind, not per address**: singles by post type; archives by kind (post type archive, taxonomy, author, date, blog home, front page); search results. Each kind is learned once from a full request, as now, and holds the plugins that kind needs on every page of it (template parts, widgets, menus and global hooks seen there).
- **A page's own content**: for singles, one direct query by path before plugins load (the approach #90 proposed) reads `post_content`; blocks and shortcodes in it are matched to the plugins that registered them (blocks through `attribute()` / `note_block()`; shortcode owners from `$shortcode_tags`, as `page_needs()` and `front_notes()` already do). A post with a form keeps the forms plugin; a post without one does not.
- **Search**: the plugins needed by the post types that can appear in results, plus global parts (FDP keeps search lists on 2 surveyed sites).
- **Unknowns load every plugin**: a page kind not learned yet, a block or shortcode no plugin was seen to register, an address no rewrite rule or post matches.
- No option writes on visitor requests except the first learn of a page kind (a bounded number), never per address. Remove the per-address list and `PAGE_LIMIT` if nothing else needs them.
- Keep the existing safety: cookie-free public GET requests only for learning, the always-load set, dependencies, the opt-out list, and the fatal-error fallback.

Per-post manual rules (FDP's "Singles") are not needed when the content decides; the opt-out list is the bypass.

## Verification

On a throwaway WordPress site (AGENTS.md → Testing, steps 2 and 4) with Kadence, WooCommerce, Fluent Forms, a plugin with its own post type and a few admin tools, and no page cache:

- After each page kind is learned once, a first visit to a never-visited post of each type skips the plugins that type does not use (one-file marker plugins or compare with `?seoprostack-load-all=1`).
- A post with a Fluent Forms block or shortcode keeps Fluent Forms; shop, product, cart, checkout and My account keep WooCommerce.
- Logged-out output of at least 14 URLs (front page, posts, pages, custom type, archives, search, shop pages) matches the full-load output, as in #90; cart and checkout work.
- Repeat visits do not write `seoprostack_plugin_front` (`wp option get` before and after, or a query log).
- Editing a post to add a form makes the next visit keep the forms plugin.
- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh`, `scripts/plugin-check.sh`; no new `debug.log` lines mentioning `seoprostack`.
