title: fix: a deleted plugin still listed as active makes features wait (Load plugins only where needed never learns)
body:
## What

A plugin whose folder was deleted while still active stays in `active_plugins` (or `active_sitewide_plugins`) until someone opens that site's Plugins screen. WordPress never loads it (`wp_get_active_and_valid_plugins()` skips missing files), but SEO Pro Stack counts it as active:

- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` `start()`: the Freesoul Deactivate Plugins check (added in ac127da, #226) returns for any `freesoul-deactivate-plugins*` entry, so **Load plugins only where needed** waits there for good, and that site never learns its pages.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-feature.php` `active_plugins()` → `replaced_active()`: every feature with `replaces` waits while a deleted replaced plugin is still listed.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php` `fdp_in_use()`: a stale Freesoul entry keeps Freesoul's must-use file, which goes on skipping plugins by Freesoul's saved rules.

## Evidence

#226 survey after deploying 1.3.7: one subsite of a network (site M) went from 70 skips to none, with every page "site not learned yet". Its `active_plugins` still lists `freesoul-deactivate-plugins-pro/freesoul-deactivate-plugins-pro.php`, but no install has Freesoul's files. The 1.3.7 update cleared the learned map, as every update does; after that, the loader returned at the Freesoul check, so nothing was learned again (no lock, no failure record, no later forget). The other 14 installs, with no such entry, learned again as usual.

## Fix

Count an entry as active only when its plugin file exists, as WordPress does (`validate_file()` and `WP_PLUGIN_DIR . '/' . $file`), in those three places. Leave `stored_active_plugins()` alone: the learned maps' fingerprints use the list as stored.

## Verification

- `composer lint` (or the repository's PHP lint) and the CI smoke tests.
- On the affected subsite after the release: an anonymous visit learns the site (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::front_current()` is true), and the next #226 survey shows site M skipping again.

title: fix: Hosting needs: no false 'did not keep a test value' warning for LiteSpeed Cache's object cache
body:
## What happens

Hosting needs (Plugins screen and Site Health) warns on a Hostinger site that uses LiteSpeed Cache's object cache (Memcached at `[::1]:11211`):

> The object cache (LiteSpeed Cache) did not keep a test value between daily checks, so it may be falling back to the database. …

The cache works. On that site:

- `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` is true, LiteSpeed Cache's drop-in is loaded, and Memcached answers at the configured host and port.
- Stored daily facts: `state => unreachable, name => LiteSpeed Cache, cause => probe`.
- Hostinger's Memcached is shared (1 GB, 92% full, `cmd_flush` 544k). LiteSpeed Cache's **Purge All**, which runs on every plugin update by default, also flushes the object cache (`Purge::_purge_all()` → `_purge_all_object()`). A test value that nobody reads for a day gets flushed or evicted, so the warning is a false alarm.

## Cause

`object_cache_facts()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` runs the cross-request test value for every drop-in, including LiteSpeed Cache's. README → Object cache health says test values are only for *other* drop-ins: LiteSpeed Cache's cache is checked by asking its configured server (`cache_server()`), which shows whether its drop-in falls back. LiteSpeed Cache's drop-in falls back only when it cannot connect.

## Fix

- In `object_cache_facts()`, skip the test value when LiteSpeed Cache's own drop-in is loaded (`LSCWP_OBJECT_CACHE`) and its server answers. Keep it for other drop-ins.
- Check once more, at once, when the stored result is a lost test value for LiteSpeed Cache, so sites showing the false warning clear it on the next admin screen and don't wait up to a day (same pattern as the existing extension recheck).
- README → Object cache health: say so.

## Verification

- `php -l`, `composer phpcs` / PHPStan on the file (project gates).
- On the Hostinger site: after updating, open Plugins; the warning is gone and `wp option get seoprostack_hosting_object_cache` shows `state => working`, with no `probe`.

title: feat: Clean up deleted plugins: Clean up every site now button for network admins
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

## What

Add a **Clean up every site now** button to the **Clean up deleted plugins** setting (Plugins tab), for network administrators on a multisite. One press checks every site on the network and removes entries for plugins whose files are gone:

- each site's `active_plugins`, plus the network's `active_sitewide_plugins`, using WordPress's own `validate_active_plugins()`, which deactivates missing plugins silently. This is what core does when someone opens that site's Plugins screen.
- each site's `uninstall_plugins` and `recently_activated`, plus the network's `recently_activated`. This reuses the feature's existing `clean_keys()`.

Afterwards a notice says how many sites were checked and which deleted plugins were removed. The on/off switch and its automatic Plugins-screen cleanup stay exactly as they are.

## Why

The automatic cleanup only runs on a site whose Plugins screen someone opens. On a network, most subsites' Plugins screens are rarely opened, so stale entries can stay there for good. #521 found exactly that: site M still listed `freesoul-deactivate-plugins-pro/…` long after its files were deleted, and **Load plugins only where needed** stopped learning there. PR #522 makes SEO Pro Stack ignore such entries, but other plugins that read `get_option('active_plugins')` directly still treat a deleted plugin as active. A super admin needs a single action that tidies the whole network.

Decision (owner, this session): keep the switch, and add the button as an extra for multisite admins. Single sites are out of scope, because there the Plugins screen is the obvious place and core already cleans `active_plugins` there.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** The feature follows an existing pattern (Database cleanup's panel with **Clean now**) inside a settled boundary (super admin only, core's own validator). The worker still has to make local choices about notice wording, the result hand-off after redirect and the site cap, so no exact oldString/newString contract is supplied.

## How (Approach)

### Progressive Context Plan

- **Read first:** `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php` (whole file, 164 lines). This is the feature being extended.
- **Read first:** `includes/features/class-seoprostack-database-cleanup.php:258-266` (`boot()` registers the panel and `admin_post_` hooks even when the feature is off), `:1037-1101` (`panel()`, with the form, nonce and button at `:1091-1099`) and `:1177-1186` (`clean_now()`: capability check, `check_admin_referer`, redirect). This is the pattern to copy.
- **Read first:** `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php:159` (`FDP_MAX_SITES = 1000`) and `:850-866` (loop over `get_sites()`, `switch_to_blog()` and `restore_current_blog()`, with a cap). This is the site-loop pattern.
- **Load only if needed:** `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:180-208` (how `'panel' => true` and the `seoprostack_setting_panel` action render), and `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php:125-141` (schema keys, including `panel`).
- **Stop when:** the panel, handler and notice are wired and the verification below passes. Read `STANDARDS.md` → code rules before editing (repository rule).

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php`: add the panel, the admin-post handler, the loop over every site and the result notice
- `EDIT: README.md:1163-1165`: describe the button in "Clean up deleted plugins (Plugins)", and add a line under `## Changelog` → `### Unreleased`
- `EDIT: changelog.txt`: add a line under `= Unreleased =`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `SEOProStack_Plugin_References` is booted through the feature registry like every other feature. `rg -n "plugin_references|Plugin_References"` finds only its own file and docs. The settings UI reads its `settings()` schema through `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php`.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** existing: `clean_up()` → `clean_keys()` on `load-plugins.php`. New: an `admin_post_seoprostack_plugin_references_network` handler that writes `active_plugins` (via core's `validate_active_plugins()` → `deactivate_plugins($file, true)`), `uninstall_plugins` and `recently_activated` on each site, and `active_sitewide_plugins` and the network `recently_activated` once.
- **Existing verification/tests:** no PHPUnit suite covers this feature (`rg -n "Plugin_References" tests` finds nothing). CI runs `composer lint` (`scripts/lint.sh`), phpcs, PHPStan level 7 and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` (single-site Docker). The production path is the button on a multisite.
- **Schemas/config:** the setting schema in `settings()` gains `'panel' => is_multisite()` so the Options panel appears on networks only. The stored value of `plugin_references` and its default do not change.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none. `git ls-files "languages/*" "*.pot"` is empty, so no tracked `.pot` file needs regenerating.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A. `git ls-files "includes/*migration*"` is empty and `rg -n "plugin_references" includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php` finds nothing, so there is no migration for this key. The button only runs when pressed and stores nothing new apart from a 5-minute per-user result transient, so existing installs need no backfill or ordering step.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** reverting the PR removes the button. Entries it removed belonged to plugins whose files no longer exist, and WordPress removes the same entries from `active_plugins` itself on the Plugins screen. If a plugin is re-uploaded later, it can be activated again normally.

### Implementation Steps

1. **Schema:** in `settings()`, add `'panel' => is_multisite(),` to the `plugin_references` entry. Leave `default`, `label`, `description` and `replaces` alone.
2. **Boot:** in `boot()`, register `seoprostack_setting_panel` → `panel` and `admin_post_` + `self::NETWORK_ACTION` → `clean_network` before the `!self::enabled()` early return, inside `is_admin() && is_multisite()`, as Database cleanup does at `:258-266`. The button works whether the switch is on or off. Keep the existing `load-plugins.php` and notice hooks behind `enabled()`.
3. **Constants:** add `const NETWORK_ACTION = 'seoprostack_plugin_references_network';` and `const MAX_SITES = 1000;` (the same cap as `SEOProStack_Plugin_Fixes::FDP_MAX_SITES`).
4. **Panel** (`panel($key, $field = array())`): return unless `self::KEY === $key`. For users without `manage_network_plugins`, print a `.sps-panel-note` saying that only network administrators can clean up every site, then return. Otherwise print one short sentence about what the button does, then a POST form to `admin-post.php` with `action=NETWORK_ACTION`, `wp_nonce_field(self::NETWORK_ACTION)` and `<button type="submit" class="button">Clean up every site now</button>`. Copy the markup from `class-seoprostack-database-cleanup.php:1091-1099`.
5. **Handler** (`clean_network()`): if `!is_multisite() || !current_user_can('manage_network_plugins') || !SEOProStack_Settings::can_change()`, call `wp_die(…, 403)`. Then `check_admin_referer(self::NETWORK_ACTION)`, and `require_once ABSPATH . 'wp-admin/includes/plugin.php'` if `validate_active_plugins` does not exist. Skeleton:

   ```php
   $removed = array();
   $sites   = get_sites(array('fields' => 'ids', 'number' => self::MAX_SITES + 1));
   $capped  = count($sites) > self::MAX_SITES;
   $sites   = array_slice($sites, 0, self::MAX_SITES);
   foreach ($sites as $site_id) {
       switch_to_blog($site_id);
       $removed = array_merge($removed, array_keys(validate_active_plugins())); // also covers active_sitewide_plugins for a network admin
       $removed = array_merge($removed, self::clean_keys('recently_activated', false), self::clean_keys('uninstall_plugins', false));
       restore_current_blog();
   }
   $removed = array_merge($removed, self::clean_keys('recently_activated', true));
   // Hand the result to the next request (per-user transient, about 5 minutes), then redirect.
   set_transient('seoprostack_plugin_refs_' . get_current_user_id(), array('files' => array_values(array_unique($removed)), 'sites' => count($sites), 'capped' => $capped), 5 * MINUTE_IN_SECONDS);
   wp_safe_redirect(admin_url('options-general.php?page=seoprostack&tab=plugins'));
   exit;
   ```

   Confirm in core that `validate_active_plugins()` returns `array( $file => WP_Error )` for the invalid entries and calls `deactivate_plugins( $plugin, true )`. Read `wp-admin/includes/plugin.php` in the test site's WordPress; do not assume.
6. **Notice:** on the next request, read and delete the transient, then print a `notice-info is-dismissible` notice. Reuse the folder-name mapping in `notice()` (lines 144-148), and extract it into a small private helper if both need it. Wording: "Checked N sites. Removed leftover entries for X deleted plugins: a, b." If nothing was found: "Checked N sites. No leftover entries for deleted plugins." If capped, add: "Only the first 1,000 sites were checked." Register it on `admin_notices` inside the same `is_multisite()` block as step 2.
7. **Docs:** README "Clean up deleted plugins (Plugins)": add a paragraph about the button (network administrators on a multisite; every site; also active entries, as the Plugins screen does; works whether the switch is on or off). Add an `Unreleased` changelog line in README.md and changelog.txt, in the house style ("New: …"). PR #522 also adds an `### Unreleased` / `= Unreleased =` heading. If it has merged, add your line under the existing heading instead of creating a second one.
8. Run `php -l` and `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the PHP file, then `composer phpstan`, and commit a WIP checkpoint before the full CI gates.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** each option is read and written once per site, the same race window core's Plugins screen has. Two admins pressing at once produce the same result, because removal is idempotent. No locking is needed.
- **Migration/rollback:** no stored shape changes. Rollback is a code revert. Removed entries belong to plugins without files, which WordPress never loads (`wp_get_active_and_valid_plugins()`).
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** the minimum is WordPress 6.2 / PHP 7.4 (smoke matrix). `validate_active_plugins()`, `get_sites()` and `deactivate_plugins($plugins, $silent)` all predate 6.2. Single sites see no change, because the panel is only added when `is_multisite()`.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a second press finds nothing and says so. A crash part-way leaves the remaining sites untouched, and pressing again finishes them.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** always call `restore_current_blog()` after each `switch_to_blog()`. Do not return from inside the loop. On networks larger than `MAX_SITES` (1000), only the first 1000 are checked and the notice says so.
- **Page learning side effect:** changing a site's `active_plugins` changes the fingerprint `SEOProStack_Feature::stored_active_plugins()` feeds to **Load plugins only where needed**, so that site learns its pages again. This is intended, and the same thing happens when core cleans the list on the Plugins screen. Only sites that actually had stale entries are affected, because `validate_active_plugins()` writes only when it finds an invalid entry. Confirm this in core while doing step 5.
- **Trust boundary:** the handler requires `manage_network_plugins`, `SEOProStack_Settings::can_change()` and a valid nonce. It never takes a plugin file or site ID from the request.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
php -l includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php
vendor/bin/phpcs includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php
composer phpstan
composer lint
# Production path, on a multisite test site (or a throwaway converted with `wp core multisite-convert`, sized per DEVELOPMENT.md → Test site resources):
wp --url=<subsite> eval 'update_option("active_plugins", array_merge((array) get_option("active_plugins"), array("gone-plugin/gone-plugin.php")));'
wp --url=<subsite> eval 'update_option("uninstall_plugins", array_merge((array) get_option("uninstall_plugins"), array("gone-plugin/gone-plugin.php" => true)));'
# As a super admin: Settings → SEO Pro Stack → Plugins → Clean up deleted plugins → Options → Clean up every site now
wp --url=<subsite> option get active_plugins --format=json      # gone-plugin absent; real plugins still listed
wp --url=<subsite> option get uninstall_plugins --format=json   # gone-plugin absent
```

- **Surface mapping:** lint, phpcs and PHPStan cover the changed PHP file. The `wp eval` setup plus the button press covers the handler, the loop over every site, `validate_active_plugins()`, `clean_keys()` and the notice (acceptance 1–3). `option get` on a real active plugin, plus a single-site check, covers the regressions (acceptance 4–5).
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required beyond the repository's normal PR CI (lint, PHPStan, smoke tests, release build).

### Recoverability Checkpoint

- [ ] Focused functional verification passes: `php -l` + `vendor/bin/phpcs` on the PHP file
- [ ] WIP commit created before broad gates: `wip: Clean up deleted plugins: button for every site`
- [ ] Repository CI (lint, PHPStan, smoke tests, release build) passes on the PR

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change the switch's default or its automatic `load-plugins.php` behaviour. Do not show the button on single sites. Do not touch `SEOProStack_Feature::stored_active_plugins()` or the plugin loader. Do not add WP-CLI commands, tests or test infrastructure. Do not write other plugins' own settings. Read `STANDARDS.md` and AGENTS.md (scope and wording rules) before changing anything.

**AI brief owner:** @marcusquinn interactive session that filed this issue.

**Recovery:** keep the PR, and use `reference/worker-discipline.md` "Integration scope recovery" if an adjacent file turns out to be needed (for example a shared notice helper).

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php`
- `README.md`
- `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] On a multisite, a network administrator sees **Clean up every site now** in the Options panel of **Clean up deleted plugins**, whether the switch is on or off. Pressing it removes a deleted plugin's entries from every site's `active_plugins`, `uninstall_plugins` and `recently_activated`, and from the network's `active_sitewide_plugins` and `recently_activated`.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "validate_active_plugins\\(\\)"
    path: "includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php"
  ```

- [ ] After pressing it, a notice says how many sites were checked and names the deleted plugins removed, or says that none were found. If the network has more than 1000 sites, it says only the first 1000 were checked.
- [ ] The handler refuses (403) users without `manage_network_plugins`, or without `SEOProStack_Settings::can_change()`, and refuses requests without a valid nonce.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: codebase
    pattern: "check_admin_referer\\(self::NETWORK_ACTION\\)"
    path: "includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php"
  ```

- [ ] Regression: entries for plugins whose files exist are never removed, and a site administrator without network rights cannot run it.
- [ ] Regression: on a single site, the setting card shows no Options panel and no button, and the automatic Plugins-screen cleanup behaves as before.
- [ ] `php -l`, phpcs, PHPStan and `composer lint` are clean, and PR CI (smoke tests on WordPress 6.2/PHP 7.4 and latest/PHP 8.3, release build and Plugin Check) passes.
- [ ] README "Clean up deleted plugins (Plugins)" and the Unreleased changelog entries in README.md and changelog.txt describe the button.

## Context & Decisions

- The owner chose in this session to keep the switch (on by default, cheap, runs only when needed) and add a button for multisite admins, rather than replace the switch with a button. A button alone needs someone to notice the problem, and nobody can see these leftovers.
- `validate_active_plugins()` is used so that core decides what is invalid, exactly as on the Plugins screen. SEO Pro Stack does not invent its own rule for `active_plugins`.
- Non-goals: single sites, WP-CLI, scheduled or background runs, and any change to #521/PR #522's internal "is it installed" checks.
- Related: #521 (stale Freesoul entry on site M) and PR #522 (SEO Pro Stack ignores deleted plugins internally).

## Relevant Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-references.php:62-79` (`boot()`, `exists()`), `:84-134` (`clean_up()`, `clean_keys()`) and `:139-163` (`notice()`)
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-database-cleanup.php:258-266`, `:1037-1101` and `:1177-1186`: panel and **Clean now** pattern
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php:159` and `:850-866`: capped loop over the network's sites
- `admin/includes/class-settings-manager.php:180-208`: Options panel and the `seoprostack_setting_panel` action
- `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php:102-110`: `can_change()`
- `README.md:1163-1165`: feature docs

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none. If PR #522 has merged first, add the changelog line under the existing Unreleased heading.
- **External:** a multisite test site for the production-path check. If none is reachable, convert a throwaway site and say so in the PR.

title: fix: Hosting needs: object cache turned on or off still shows the old result for up to a day
body:
## What happens

Hosting needs keeps showing "Memcached is available on this server but the site is not using it" for up to a day after the object cache is turned on.

Seen on a Hostinger test site with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 and SEO Pro Stack 1.3.7: the daily check ran (`checked` 1791243095) 27 seconds before LiteSpeed Cache wrote `wp-content/object-cache.php` (mtime 1791243122). The stored result `{"state":"off","available":"Memcached"}` was then shown all day, although `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` was true and a test value was kept. Deleting `seoprostack_hosting_object_cache` gave `state: working` at once.

The same happens the other way: a cache turned off, or a drop-in removed, keeps showing "working" for up to a day.

## Fix

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` → `object_cache_facts()`: check again before the day is out when the stored state no longer matches `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` in this request (stored `off` but in use now, or stored `working` but not in use now). The call is free, and the check still runs only from the admin, cron or WP-CLI. Put it in `recheck_cache()`, which PR #525 (GH#524) adds, so this stacks on that branch.

Also update README.md → Hosting needs → Object cache health and changelog.txt → Unreleased.

## Verification

- `composer lint` / PHPCS and PHPStan as CI runs them.
- On the test site: store `{"state":"off","checked":<now>}` in `seoprostack_hosting_object_cache` with the cache on, then run `wp eval 'echo json_encode(SEOProStack_Hosting_Needs::facts()["object_cache"]);'`. It should report `working`.

title: fix: Hosting needs: PHP workers from average time per request, not p95
body:
## What happens

Hosting needs sizes PHP workers with Little's law (requests per second in a burst × time per request), but it uses the p95 page time, rounded up to the top of its timing slot (`BUCKETS` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`). The busiest-hour (×3) and burst (×3) factors already cover peaks, so p95 counts the slow-request margin twice. The slot rounding inflates it further: anything from 2 to 4 s becomes 4.00.

Live example (Hostinger site, 3 days, 1,678 samples): busiest hour 1,760 requests; page p95 slot top 4.00 s, page average 1.17 s, average of all requests 2.0 s. **Now** shows 7 workers and 8 CPU cores. With the average it would be 4 workers and 4 cores.

## Fix

- `SEOProStack_Hosting_Needs::traffic()`: return the average for pages (once there are enough samples) and for all requests.
- `assess()`: **Now** uses the average of all sampled requests, because the busiest-hour count includes admin, REST API and cron requests, which hold workers too. Low, medium and high use the average visitor page time, because admin and cron don't grow with visits (owner's rule from GH#66).
- `SEOProStack_Hosting_Plans::plans()`: accept the time for Now separately.
- The traffic text shows the averages and keeps the p95 page figure as information.
- README → Hosting to buy, changelog.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- On a site with samples: Now workers = ceil(requests per second in a burst × average time) + 1.

title: Pinned posts: 'Pin from a true/false field' is silently cleared when settings are saved without ACF loaded
body:
## What happened

On a production site using Pinned posts → **Pin from a true/false field** (`sticky_posts_fields`, added in #355), the setting was found empty (`[]`) about a day after it was set to `awards|featured_listing`. No one cleared it on purpose. While it was empty, ticking the ACF field on an award no longer pinned it (73 featured items, 72 pinned). Restoring the value re-synced the pins.

## Cause (from the 1.3.7 code)

- `sticky_posts_fields` is a `multi` setting without `open`, so `SEOProStack_Settings::sanitize_multi()` keeps only values present in `options_for($field)`.
- Its options come from `SEOProStack_Sticky_Posts::field_options()` → `true_false_fields()`, which returns `[]` when `acf_get_field_groups()` / `acf_get_fields()` do not exist or no field groups are registered yet on that request (ACF not loaded, e.g. skipped by plugin loading, or before `acf/init`). The result is also cached in a `static`.
- `sanitize_all()` runs on **every** `update_option('seoprostack_options')`: a save of any other setting (`ajax_save()`), a DB migration (`maybe_migrate()`), `set()`. On such a request the stored `type|field` value is not "known" and is silently dropped.
- Making the field `open` alone does not help: the open-list regex `/^[A-Za-z0-9_\\-]+$/` rejects the `|` in `awards|featured_listing`.

## Expected

A setting whose options cannot be computed on the current request keeps its stored value, the same way `sanitize_all()` already keeps settings of features that are not registered on the request.

## Suggested fix

Files: `includes/class-seoprostack-settings.php` (`sanitize_multi()`, `sanitize_all()`), `includes/features/class-seoprostack-sticky-posts.php` (`settings()` → `sticky_posts_fields`).

Options, in order of preference:

1. In `sanitize_multi()`, when `options_for($field)` is empty (options unavailable on this request), return the stored value for that key instead of `[]`. Generic, protects every callable-options `multi`.
2. Or allow `|` in the open-list identifier regex and mark `sticky_posts_fields` as `open`, so `type|field_name` survives; `linked_fields()` already ignores fields that do not exist.

## Verification

- With `sticky_posts_fields = ["awards|featured_listing"]`, save another SEO Pro Stack setting in a request where ACF is not loaded (or call `SEOProStack_Settings::sanitize_all()` with ACF functions unavailable): the value must remain.
- With ACF loaded, deselecting the field in the UI must still clear it.
- `count(get_option('sticky_posts'))` for the type matches the number of posts with the field on after `match_fields()`.

Unknown: which exact request cleared it on the affected site (no access logs on that host); the window was between a verified-correct state and an editor save one day later.

title: feat: Hosting needs: say when the PHP memory limit is far above what the site uses
body:
## What

Hosting needs reports "PHP memory has room" whenever the highest use is under 80% of `memory_limit` (`assess_memory()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`). It says nothing when the limit is far above anything the site uses.

Seen on a Hostinger site: `memory_limit` 12 GB, highest use in 7 days 384 MB, and the table's own suggestion is 768M. A limit that high lets one runaway request (a stuck import, a plugin loop) use most of the server's RAM before PHP stops it. Other requests then slow down or the server swaps, instead of that one request failing with a clear error.

## Proposal

- In `assess_memory()`: when the limit is more than 4 times `memory_limit_need()` and above 2 GB, add an `info` line (not a warning): "PHP's memory limit is %1$s, but no request used more than %2$s in 7 days. A lower limit, such as %3$s, stops a runaway request before it uses the server's memory." Use the same `LIMIT_STEPS` value the table suggests.
- Keep it `info`: hosts set this, and a high limit isn't a fault on its own.
- Site Health Info: no change (the limit and peaks are already listed).

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: `assess_memory()`, `memory_limit_need()` (reference pattern for the suggested value).
- README → Hosting needs (PHP memory), changelog.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- On a site with `memory_limit` = -1 or 12G: the info line shows on the Plugins screen row and in Site Health. With -1 (unlimited), say "no limit".

title: fix: correct the update count in the admin menu; Load plugins only where needed keeps update data complete
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# Correct the update count in the admin menu; Load plugins only where needed keeps update data complete

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `update count admin menu stale updates transient` → 0 hits
- [x] Discovery pass: no open or recent issues/PRs about the update count (`gh issue list --search "updates count menu"`: #512, #164, #7, all unrelated)
- [x] File refs verified against WordPress core on the preview site (`wp-includes/update.php`, `wp-admin/admin.php`, `wp-admin/menu.php`)
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard`
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision: skipped, implemented in the owner's interactive session

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-06
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (owner session)
- **Conversation context:** The owner sometimes sees a number next to Dashboard › Updates, but the Updates screen then says everything is up to date. The owner asked for all three fixes below.

## What

1. **Correct the update count** (new feature, Admin tab, on by default as safe on any site). Filter `wp_get_update_data` (core, `wp-includes/update.php:1021`) so the counts in the admin menu (Updates, Plugins, Appearance) and the admin bar leave out updates that are already installed:
   - plugins: the plugin file is gone, or its installed version differs from the version the stored check was made with (`checked`) and is at least the offered `new_version`;
   - themes: the same with `wp_get_theme()`;
   - WordPress: the stored check was made for another version (`version_checked`) and the offer is not newer than the running version.
   Titles (the menu bubble's tooltip) are rebuilt to match. Nothing in WordPress's update data, checks or schedule changes; only the displayed numbers.
2. **Load plugins only where needed: no update check with skipped plugins.** `_maybe_update_core/_plugins/_themes` run on `admin_init` every 12 hours on any admin screen, including screens that skip plugins, so updaters of skipped plugins (`pre_set_site_transient_update_*`) are missing from the saved check. When one of the three checks is due, the loader loads every plugin on that request (new reason `updates`, said in the admin bar). At most once an hour, so sites where checks never run (updates switched off) do not load every plugin on every screen.
3. **Load plugins only where needed: counts from a screen with every plugin.** Some plugins add their updates when the stored check is read (Kadence Blocks via StellarWP Harbor, SliceWP: `site_transient_update_plugins` filters). On screens that skip them the number is too low. Requests that load every plugin keep the plugin and theme updates they see (small non-autoloaded option, written only when it changes); screens that skip plugins add those that are not installed yet.

## Why

- Core's `wp_get_update_data()` (`update.php:935`) counts the stored check as it is. The menu is built at `wp-admin/admin.php:163` before `load-update-core.php` (`admin.php:390`) refreshes the check, and other screens refresh only every 12 hours. Updates made outside WordPress's updater (host updates, Git or SFTP deploys, folders deleted) leave entries behind until then.
- The loader is SEO Pro Stack's own: it must not make the update data or count incomplete.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `NEW: includes/features/class-seoprostack-update-count.php`: the feature (model: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-admin-tidy.php`)
- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php:30`: register in `FEATURES`, after `SEOProStack_Admin_Tidy`
- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php:480-489`: `updates` reason before `self::filter()`
- `EDIT: includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php:3225`: admin bar text for `updates`
- `EDIT: uninstall.php:119`: new options
- `EDIT: README.md`, `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `wp_get_update_data()` callers: `wp-admin/menu.php:38,214,313`, `wp_admin_bar_updates_menu()`; loader `start()` (must-use file, before plugins load).
- **Writers/mutation paths:** two new non-autoloaded options: the counts snapshot (written only when it changes, on requests with every plugin loaded) and the loader's last forced full request (at most once an hour).
- **Existing verification/tests:** none cover update counts (`rg -n "wp_get_update_data" includes` → no hits before this change); verify on a real site.
- **Schemas/config:** one new bool setting `update_count`, default true.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** the must-use file loads `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` directly; no copy to regenerate.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A, a new setting follows its default on existing sites (`STANDARDS.md` → Structure).
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** `uninstall.php` option list.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Plugin Check:** never name `site_transient_update_*` or `pre_set_site_transient_update_*` in code or comments (`plugin_updater_detected`). Read with `get_site_transient('update_plugins')`.
- **Update behaviour:** `STANDARDS.md` forbids changing update transients or checks; the feature changes only displayed counts, and the loader only loads more plugins.
- **Performance:** only response entries are checked (one `get_file_data()` per listed plugin, cached per request); the loader's due check reads the three site transients that core reads on the same request anyway.
- **PHP 7.4 / WP 6.2:** `wp_get_update_data` filter and `get_core_updates()` exist; guard `get_core_updates` with `function_exists` as core does.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
./scripts/lint.sh
# Preview or throwaway site: put a stale entry in the stored plugin check (wp eval), open the Dashboard: Updates shows no number;
# switch the feature off: the number is back. With Load plugins only where needed, set update_plugins last_checked 13 h back:
# the next screen loads every plugin (admin bar says why) and last_checked is refreshed.
```

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-update-count.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- `uninstall.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stored update for a plugin that is already at or past the offered version, or no longer installed, is not counted in the Updates, Plugins or admin bar numbers.
- [ ] Negative: an update the stored check offers for a plugin that has not changed since the check still counts; WordPress's update data is never written.
- [ ] With Load plugins only where needed, an admin screen where an update check is due loads every plugin, at most once an hour.
- [ ] With Load plugins only where needed, updates added by skipped plugins still count on screens that skip them, and stop counting once installed.
- [ ] `scripts/lint.sh` passes; Plugin Check finds no updater code.

title: fix: Hosting needs: object cache checked from WP-CLI or command-line cron can report another PHP's cache
body:
## What happens

On a Hostinger site whose web PHP is 8.1 while the account's command-line PHP (`/usr/bin/php`, used by WP-CLI and hPanel cron jobs) is 8.5, visitors had no object cache: PHP 8.1 did not load `memcached`, so `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` was false on every web request. WP-CLI and the cron job ran PHP 8.5, which loads `memcached`, so there the cache worked.

Hosting needs runs its daily object cache check from the admin, cron or WP-CLI. On this site the cron job runs every minute from the command line, so the stored result came from PHP 8.5 and could say `working` for a day while the site's pages had no cache; an admin visit after a stale day would say the opposite. The same happens the other way (cache only on the web PHP: a false warning from cron).

Checked from the web with a temporary PHP file on each of 14 Hostinger sites: 13 used Memcached; this one (PHP 8.1) did not, although WP-CLI reported it working on all 14.

## Cause

`object_cache_facts()` in `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php` checks on `is_admin() || wp_doing_cron() || WP_CLI`. Cron run from the command line and WP-CLI can use a different PHP (version, extensions, ini) from the one serving the site. `live_sapi()` already tells the command line apart for How PHP runs (#517).

## Fix

- `object_cache_facts()`: check only on web requests (`'' !== self::live_sapi()`): admin screens, Site Health and cron started over HTTP. The command line returns the stored result.
- Docblock, README.md → Hosting needs → Object cache health, changelog.txt → Unreleased.

PR #529 (GH#528) rechecks when the stored state disagrees with `wp_using_ext_object_cache()` in this request; with this guard that comparison only happens on web requests, so CLI cron cannot flip it back.

## Verification

- `composer lint` / PHPCS and PHPStan as CI runs them; `php -l`.
- On a site where CLI and web PHP differ: `wp option delete seoprostack_hosting_object_cache`, run `wp eval 'echo json_encode(SEOProStack_Hosting_Needs::facts()["object_cache"]);'` → `unknown` (not checked); open the Plugins screen → the stored result matches the web PHP.

title: fix: Tutor LMS Certificate Builder logs PHP warnings on every update check
body:
## What happens

Tutor LMS Certificate Builder 1.3.2 ships the same Themeum updater as Tutor LMS Pro (`updater/update.php`, class `TutorCB\ThemeumUpdater\Update`). Extend it to Certificate Builder (product slug `tutor-lms-certificate-builder`, version constant `TUTOR_CB_VERSION`), filling in the installed version and no download address. Replies that offer an update stay as they are.

Files: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php` (fix, header comment, setting description), `README.md` → Fixes for other plugins and Changelog, `changelog.txt`.

## What

Add a **Fixes for other plugins** entry for Burst Statistics 3.7.2: its `upgrade_lookup_tables` database upgrade fails on every run with "Illegal mix of collations" when `{prefix}burst_statistics` has a different collation from its lookup tables. The upgrade never finishes, and it adds the same database error to the PHP log every 5 minutes, indefinitely.

## Evidence (observed 2026-10-06, read-only checks)

- One Hostinger site (call it site E; MariaDB 11.8.9, database default `utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci`) logged the error **864 times since 2026-10-03 02:25 UTC**, about every 5 minutes, from `burst_upgrade_iteration` cron:

  ```text
  WordPress database error Illegal mix of collations (utf8mb4_unicode_ci,IMPLICIT) and (utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci,IMPLICIT) for operation '=' for query UPDATE wp_burst_statistics AS t JOIN ( SELECT p.platform, p.ID, COALESCE(m.ID, 0) as platform_id FROM wp_burst_statistics p LEFT JOIN wp_burst_platforms m ON p.platform = m.name WHERE p.platform_id = 999999 LIMIT 100000 ) AS s ON t.ID = s.ID SET t.platform_id = s.platform_id; made by ... Burst\Admin\DB_Upgrade\DB_Upgrade->upgrade, ...->upgrade_lookup_tables
  ```

- On site E, `wp_burst_statistics` (table and its `browser`, `browser_version`, `device`, `platform` columns) is `utf8mb4_unicode_ci` (created long ago), while `wp_burst_browsers`, `wp_burst_browser_versions`, `wp_burst_devices` and `wp_burst_platforms` (`name`) are `utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci` (created by the upgrade with the database default). 3,680 of 22,155 rows still have `*_id = 999999` for all four items.
- The other 10 Hostinger sites with Burst 3.7.2 have no pending rows and no old text columns, so they are not affected.
- Burst's code: `includes/Admin/DB_Upgrade/class-db-upgrade.php` `upgrade_lookup_tables()` (around line 2065 in 3.7.2). Its loop picks the **last** armed item (`platform`) each run, so `browser`, `browser_version` and `device` never get their turn either; the `LEFT JOIN ... ON p.{item} = m.name` is the failing comparison. Columns are dropped only after it finishes (`upgrade_lookup_tables_drop_columns()`, ~line 2286), so site E keeps the old text columns too.

## Proposal

In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`, the same kind of narrow fix as `tutor_create_queries()` (a `dbdelta_create_queries` filter that changes only Tutor's statements):

- Add a `query` filter, registered only while Burst Statistics is active and its option `burst_db_upgrade_upgrade_lookup_tables` exists (so it costs nothing otherwise), that matches only Burst's lookup-upgrade `UPDATE {prefix}burst_statistics AS t JOIN (... LEFT JOIN {prefix}burst_{item}s m ON p.{item} = m.name ...)` statement (`{item}` one of browser, browser_version, device, platform) and appends `COLLATE <the lookup table's name collation>` to `m.name`'s side, or `p.{item}`'s, so both sides compare in one collation. Read the lookup column's collation once per request from `information_schema.COLUMNS` (cache it in a static); leave the query unchanged if the collations already match, the charset differs (COLLATE needs the same charset), or the pattern does not match exactly.
- Do not ALTER Burst's tables: SEO Pro Stack does not change other plugins' schema here, and the rewritten join lets Burst finish and drop the old columns itself.
- Document it in README → Fixes for other plugins (with the Burst version), README Unreleased changelog and `changelog.txt`, in the house style of the Tutor LMS entries.
- Consider reporting the bug to Burst Statistics' maintainers (the CREATE TABLE for lookup tables should use the statistics table's collation, or the join should specify one); note it in the PR if reported.

## Files

Where: `class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php` `boot()` near line 270, with new private helpers next to `tutor_create_queries()` near line 607; README → Fixes for other plugins near line 1208 and the changelog's Unreleased section; `changelog.txt` Unreleased.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- Docker test site with Burst Statistics 3.7.2 on MariaDB: create `wp_burst_statistics` text columns as `utf8mb4_unicode_ci` and lookup tables as `utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci` (or `ALTER TABLE ... CONVERT TO` on a seeded site), set some rows' `*_id` to 999999, arm the upgrade option, run `wp cron event run burst_upgrade_iteration` repeatedly. Without the fix: the collation error in `debug.log`. With it: no error, pending counts fall to 0 for all four items, and Burst drops the old columns and clears `burst_db_upgrade_upgrade_lookup_tables`.
- Regression: with matching collations the query string is unchanged (log it in the test), and with Burst inactive the filter is not registered.
- After release, on site E: the error stops appearing in the PHP log and pending rows reach 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Burst's lookup-table upgrade completes on a site whose statistics table and lookup tables differ in collation, with no database errors.
- [ ] No other query is changed; nothing runs when Burst is inactive or its upgrade is not armed.
- [ ] README and both changelogs describe the fix.

title: feat: Dark mode image contrast for transparent logos and icons
body:
## What

New feature, off by default (Media tab): **Dark mode image contrast**. With the Kadence Pro dark mode switcher (body class `color-switch-dark`), transparent logos, icons and line art whose colours have too little contrast against the background they actually sit on are recoloured with a CSS filter, only while dark mode is on. Photos and opaque images are left alone.

## Why

On a live Kadence site, client logo walls and icons made for a light page disappear in dark mode: a dark-blue logo had 93% of its visible pixels below 3:1 contrast against the dark section behind it. Kadence only offers a separate dark logo for the site header; content images have no equivalent, and owners would need a dark copy of every image.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-dark-image-contrast.php` (pattern: `class-seoprostack-kadence-filters.php`, `class-seoprostack-translatepress-colours.php`): bool setting, `boot()` returns early unless enabled and on the front end; a late `body_class` filter notes whether the theme draws a `color-switch-*` class; the script is enqueued on `wp_footer` (before footer scripts print) only then. Registered in `SEOProStack_Setup::FEATURES`.
- `assets/dark-image-contrast.js` (no dependencies): runs only while `body.color-switch-dark` is set, follows switches with a MutationObserver, analyses images lazily (IntersectionObserver) and re-analyses on `load` (lazy loaders, `srcset`).
  - Skips JPEGs, images with their own CSS filter, cross-origin images it cannot read, `.kadence-dark-mode-logo`, `<picture>` with a colour-scheme source and anything inside `.seoprostack-keep-colours`.
  - Draws the image at most 96 px on its longest side. Images with under 5% transparent pixels (photos, logos on a white box) are left alone. Only visible pixels count, so transparent margins in the file do not skew the result; images with many colours (cut-out photos, gradients) are left alone.
  - Finds the real background: starts at the image itself (its own background shows through and in its padding), then walks up its ancestors, compositing translucent background colours and absolutely positioned overlays (Kadence row overlays, Cover block backgrounds) that cover it. A background image or video anywhere in that stack means unknown: leave the image alone.
  - Simulates three filters on the sampled pixels (invert with hue kept, white, black), prefers the one that keeps colours, and applies one only when it makes most of the image readable at 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) and clearly improves on the original.
  - The filter is a `data-` attribute matched by CSS scoped to `body.color-switch-dark`, so switching back to light restores the original instantly.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- On a Kadence Pro site with dark mode: in light mode nothing changes; in dark mode low-contrast transparent logos become readable, photos and opaque images unchanged, `.seoprostack-keep-colours` respected; toggling back to light restores originals. Checked in Chromium and WebKit with rendered-pixel contrast probes.
- Docs: `README.md` (feature section, Unreleased), `changelog.txt` (Unreleased), `readme.txt` (one short line, file under 10 KB).

title: Load plugins only where needed: the saved menu copy brings back removed entries of loaded plugins
body:
## What happens

With **Load plugins only where needed** on, `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::restore_menu()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`, around lines 2979–3102) puts back entries from the saved admin menu copy (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::MENU`, option `seoprostack_plugin_menu`, written by `capture_menu()` around line 974) on screens that skip plugins.

It also puts back copied entries for plugins that **are loaded** on the screen. When such a plugin has since removed or moved a menu entry, the old entry comes back:

- The removed submenu entry shows again in the plugin's menu, next to its replacement (two "Settings" items).
- `$copy['hooks']` and `$copy['handled']` re-register the old page hook with the `__return_null` stand-in. The old address then opens a blank screen (200) instead of reaching `admin_page_access_denied`, where a plugin could redirect it.

The copy is dropped by `forget()` on plugin updates through WordPress (upgrader hooks), so this shows when plugin code changes another way: a deploy that copies files (Git, rsync, SFTP, a preview build), or a plugin whose menu depends on its own settings. It lasts until a screen that loads every plugin captures the copy again.

Seen on a local test site: a plugin moved its settings screen from Settings into its own top-level menu and dropped a submenu link to the old address. Every admin screen showed both the old and the new Settings items, and the old address opened a blank screen. Dropping `seoprostack_plugin_menu` fixed it.

## What to change

In `restore_menu()`, put back only what belongs to plugins skipped on this screen:

- Skip copied top-level and submenu entries, page hooks (`$copy['hooks']`), handlers (`$copy['handled']`), `admin_page_hooks` and `parents` whose owning plugin is loaded now. Its own registrations this request are authoritative.
- Ownership: check whether `capture_menu()` already records which plugin owns each page (the admin menu feature has a similar lookup, `SEOProStack_Admin_Menu::owner()` / `folder_for_callback()`). If it doesn't, record each entry's plugin folder at capture time. The list of loaded plugins comes from `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::state()`.
- If ownership is unknown for an entry, keep today's behaviour.

## Verify

1. On a test site with Load plugins only where needed on, open a screen that loads every plugin, so the copy is saved.
2. In a plugin that stays loaded on a screen that skips others (Dashboard), remove one of its submenu entries, changing its files directly (no update through WordPress).
3. Open the Dashboard: the removed entry must not appear, and its old `admin.php?page=…` / `options-general.php?page=…` address must not open a blank screen.
4. Entries of plugins skipped on that screen must still appear and open their pages.
5. `scripts/lint.sh` and `scripts/smoke-test.sh` pass.

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

Implementation uses the existing page_owners callback lookup to save page and hook ownership with the menu copy, then excludes loaded owners from every restoration path. Unknown ownership retains the current fallback. Verify with scripts/lint.sh, scripts/smoke-test.sh and a disposable WordPress direct-file menu-change reproduction. PHP minimum remains 7.4; WordPress minimum remains 6.2.

title: Readabler colours: follow the Kadence palette and dark mode
body:
## What

New feature **Readabler colours** (Content tab, off by default, like TranslatePress switcher colours): Readabler's accessibility button and popup take their colours from the Kadence palette, so they follow Kadence's light and dark mode switcher.

## Why

Readabler 2.0.18 stores fixed colours. It prints the popup's colours on `:root` and chooses its light or dark popup colours with `@media (prefers-color-scheme)`, so it follows the visitor's system setting, not the site's switcher. It also works out the translucent key colours from `rgba()` text (`FrontStyles::getTransparentColor()`). Putting palette variables into Readabler's settings would therefore keep the light values in the popup (STANDARDS.md → Front-end styling and dark mode), and it would break the translucent shades. A preset cannot do it.

The owner's colours on a live site are the site's own palette colours: button palette 5 with palette 1 on hover, icon palette 9, popup key colour palette 5.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-readabler-colours.php`, modelled on `class-seoprostack-translatepress-colours.php`. Inline CSS goes on Readabler's own `mdp-readabler` style handle, so it prints only where Readabler does. Rules are on `body` and `body .mdp-readabler-trigger-button-box` / `body #mdp-readabler-voice-navigation`, which beat Readabler's `:root` and element rules.
- Button: background `--global-palette5`, hover `--global-palette1`, icon `--global-palette9`. Popup: background `--global-palette9`, text `--global-palette4`, key `--global-palette5`. Light and dark variables get the same values, so the palette decides whichever system setting the visitor has. Translucent key colours use `color-mix()`.
- Each palette variable falls back to Readabler's own stored colour, so nothing changes without a Kadence palette.
- Register the feature in `SEOProStack::features()`. Docs: README.md (feature section and changelog), readme.txt, changelog.txt, and the Readabler preset notes.

- `php -l`, phpcs, phpstan.

title: Comment counts stay after spam comments are deleted
body:
## What

Posts keep showing a comment count after their spam comments are deleted. On a live site, 130 posts showed counts (41, 45, 34…) with no comments left; Count terms and comments in the background is on.

## Why

WordPress recounts a post only when an *approved* comment is deleted (`wp_delete_comment()`), so a stored count that is already wrong stays wrong when the spam, pending or binned comments under it are deleted. Evidence from the site:

- `wp_posts.comment_count` > 0 on 130 posts while `wp_comments` holds no comments for them; the comments were deleted permanently by an administrator (2,439 on one day, 273 later).
- Comment moderation is on, so the deleted comments were not approved; no recount ran.
- The background recount queue itself works: queueing post 8963 (count 41, no comments) and running `seoprostack_deferred_counts` set it to 0.
- `class-seoprostack-deferred-counts.php` was added after the first deletion, so it did not cause the drift; WordPress gives no way to repair it.

## How

`includes/features/class-seoprostack-deferred-counts.php`:

- When a comment that was not approved is deleted, check its post's stored count once per request (one indexed `COUNT(*)`) and recount it, through the queue, only when it is wrong, so spam deletion fixes counts without purging caches of posts whose counts are right.
- **Recount now** also finds posts (types that support comments) whose stored count does not match their approved comments, and recounts them. Post types without comment support are left alone (an anti-malware plugin stores other data in `comment_count` of its quarantine posts).

Docs: `README.md` (Count terms and comments in the background), `readme.txt`, `changelog.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` clean.
- On a test site: delete a spam comment from a post with a wrong stored count → count corrected after the background run; Recount now corrects existing wrong counts; a post type without comment support keeps its value.
- On the live site after release: wrong counts = 0 (`comment_count` vs approved comments), quarantine post untouched.

title: Trim readme.txt under 10 KB for WordPress.org
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# Trim readme.txt under 10 KB for WordPress.org

## Pre-flight (auto-populated by briefing workflow)

- [x] Memory recall: `readme.txt size 10 KB wordpress.org seoprostack` → 0 hits — no relevant lessons
- [x] Discovery pass: last readme.txt commits on main are release/feature changelog edits (5ad47c1 GH#585, 0a9b396 GH#580, ffc8e93 GH#580); no open PR is trimming readme.txt
- [x] File refs verified: `readme.txt`, `STANDARDS.md:114-118`, `RELEASING.md:44-50`, `scripts/preflight-release.sh` present at origin/main 5ad47c1
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — wording choices about which lines to shorten remain, so no exact oldString/newString contract
- [x] Seeded draft PR decision recorded: skipped — a pure wording trim; a seed would anchor the worker to arbitrary cuts

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-07
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (follow-up from the GH#585 / PR #586 release session)
- **Conversation context:** The 1.3.18 release preflight warned that `readme.txt` is 10,317 bytes. It was already 10,234 bytes at 1.3.17, so this predates GH#585. The owner asked to file it as a task.

## What

`readme.txt` (the WordPress.org readme) is under 10 KB (10,240 bytes), with headroom for future one-line changelog entries: target **at most 9,700 bytes**. Nothing a WordPress.org reader needs is lost: every feature group keeps a short line, every service the plugin contacts stays under **External services**, and the **Built with AI** credits stay.

## Why

`STANDARDS.md:116-118` and `RELEASING.md:49-50` require `readme.txt` to stay under 10 KB, because WordPress.org says larger readmes may cause errors. `scripts/preflight-release.sh` warns, and `--strict` (used for the WordPress.org submission, `RELEASING.md` → Submitting) fails on it. Each version goes to WordPress.org 30 days after its GitHub release, so fix this before then.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Tier rationale:** a single-file docs edit, but the worker has to decide which wording to shorten. No exact replacement text is supplied.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: readme.txt` — shorten the Description subsections and the FAQ; leave the header block, External services, Built with AI and the changelog section as they are, apart from wording.

### Complete Write Surface

- **Callers/readers:** `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (size check, changelog check at line 335: the `== Changelog ==` section must still contain `= X.Y.Z =` for the current version), `scripts/build-release.sh` (ships the file in both zips), and WordPress.org's readme parser. The settings screen's Read Me tab renders `README.md`, not `readme.txt` (`AGENTS.md`), so the tab does not change.
- **Writers/mutation paths:** only hand edits; releases add one changelog line (`RELEASING.md:44-50`).
- **Existing verification/tests:** `scripts/preflight-release.sh` (readme size, name, short description ≤150 characters, tags, Stable tag, changelog entries, credits check "README.md and readme.txt credit aidevops and the starter", External services hosts note).
- **Schemas/config:** WordPress.org readme format (`=== Name ===` header, `== Section ==`, `= Sub =`); keep every header field.
- **Generated/deployed mirrors:** none. Release zips are built from Git at tag time.
- **Migrations/backfills:** N/A — documentation only, verified by `rg` finding no code reading readme.txt beyond the scripts above.
- **Cleanup/rollback paths:** revert the commit.

### Implementation Steps

1. Measure: `wc -c readme.txt` (10,317 bytes at origin/main 5ad47c1). Approximate size per section at that commit:

   ```text
     448  === SEO Pro Stack === (header: keep)
     395  == Description == intro
     932  = A calmer, faster admin =
     505  = Safer logins and access =
    1269  = Writing and publishing =
     550  = Media =
    1448  = Links and speed =
     575  = Plugins and set-up =
     187  = Affiliate disclosure =
    2106  = External services = (keep every service; tighten wording only)
     319  = Built with AI = (keep the credits as they are)
     112  == Installation ==
     ~1070 == Frequently Asked Questions == (5 entries)
     184  == Screenshots == (keep the 3 captions: preflight checks them)
     ~217  == Changelog == (already only the newest version)
   ```

2. Shorten the biggest Description subsections first (Links and speed, Writing and publishing, A calmer, faster admin) to one short line per feature, as `STANDARDS.md:116-117` says. Details already live in `README.md` → Features; do not move text into README.md.
3. Tighten FAQ answers where they repeat the Description.
4. Keep plain, short sentences in the existing style. No new claims, no feature renames: names must match the settings labels in the code.
5. Run the verification below.

### Hazards and Compatibility

- **Concurrency/atomicity:** other open PRs add changelog lines at the top of `== Changelog ==`. Merge `origin/main` before merging; `scripts/preview-site.sh` keeps both sides of changelog conflicts.
- **Migration/rollback:** none; revert the commit.
- **Mixed-version/backward compatibility:** N/A — WordPress.org reads only the tagged version's readme.
- **Idempotency/retry:** a re-run is a no-op once under the target.
- **Partial failure/recovery:** a single-file commit.

### Verification Before Dispatch

```bash
wc -c readme.txt                      # ≤ 9700
scripts/preflight-release.sh          # readme.txt section: no "size ... over 10 KB" warning; 0 errors
```

- **Surface mapping:** `wc -c` proves the size target; the preflight proves the header, changelog, screenshots, credits and External services checks still pass.
- **Broad verification trigger:** not required (one documentation file).

### Files Scope

- `readme.txt`

### Scope Boundaries

**Hard boundaries:** do not change `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, the version or Stable tag, or any code. Do not remove a service from **External services** or the **Built with AI** credits.

**AI brief owner:** the interactive maintainer session for wpallstars/seoprostack.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `readme.txt` is at most 9,700 bytes.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "test $(wc -c < readme.txt) -le 9700"
  ```

- [ ] `scripts/preflight-release.sh` reports 0 errors and no readme.txt size warning.

  ```yaml
  verify:
    method: bash
    run: "scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline 2>&1 | grep -q '0 error(s)' && ! scripts/preflight-release.sh --offline 2>&1 | grep -q 'over 10 KB'"
  ```

title: feat: LiteSpeed Cache preset sets up the crawler to prime the cache after purges
body:
## What

The LiteSpeed Cache preset turns on LiteSpeed Cache's crawler on LiteSpeed servers that allow it, so pages are put back in the page cache after a purge (plugin, theme and core updates purge the whole cache, as the preset sets) and most visitors get cached pages.

## Why

On a live Hostinger site the crawler was on but only re-crawled every 3.5 days (LiteSpeed Cache's default Crawl Interval, 302400 s), so after each update purge most pages stayed uncached for days. Its last full crawl warmed about 1,050 pages for each of the desktop and mobile crawlers (Miss = crawled and cached), and LiteSpeed answers 201 to the crawler for pages already cached, so a crawl of a warm site costs little. The preset's notes also said the crawler needs QUIC.cloud; in LiteSpeed Cache 7.x it does not (it needs only the server's permission, `X-LSCACHE` containing `crawler`, and a sitemap).

## How

- `presets/litespeed-cache.json`: `litespeed.conf.crawler` on, `crawler-crawl_interval` 86400 (daily), `crawler-sitemap` worked out per site; `when` limits them to single sites on a LiteSpeed server where the crawler is allowed and a sitemap is known. Notes and `settings` labels updated.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: a `litespeed_crawler` preset condition (LiteSpeed Cache's own `Router::can_crawl()` plus a known sitemap) and a `seoprostack_plugin_presets` filter that fills the sitemap: one already set in LiteSpeed Cache stays; otherwise Rank Math's or Yoast's sitemap index, else WordPress's own (`get_sitemap_url('index')`); `seoprostack_crawler_sitemap` filter for others.
- Saves go through LiteSpeed Cache's `Conf::update_confs()` as before, which schedules its crawler cron.
- Server IP stays out of the preset (site-specific; a wrong one stops the crawler).
- Changelog lines in `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`; `docs/presets.md` owner decision.

## Verification

- `php -l`, PHPCS (project config), `scripts/preflight-release.sh` or `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`.
- On a LiteSpeed test site: `wp seoprostack presets diff litespeed-cache` shows the three crawler settings with the site's sitemap; `apply` stores them and `wp cron event list` shows `litespeed_task_crawler`; `reset` and `undo` put them back.

title: fix: LiteSpeed Cache crawler turns end before the host's 300-second request limit
body:
## What

Fixes for other plugins gives LiteSpeed Cache's crawler turns of 240 seconds (its `LITESPEED_CRAWLER_DURATION` constant, unless the site defines it), so each turn finishes before the host stops the request.

## Why

LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 plans 900-second crawler turns. It raises `max_execution_time` to 915 (`Crawler::_engine_start()`), but Hostinger's LiteSpeed server ends PHP requests at 300 seconds whatever PHP allows. A probe straight to the origin got HTTP 503 at 301 s, with its heartbeat stopping at 300 s. Evidence from a live site after #588:

- The turn started at 01:20:13. The crawler's last position update was at 01:25:06, and its lane file (`wp-content/litespeed/crawler/meta.data.pid`) was last touched at 01:25:13, exactly 300 s in. `is_running` was never cleared.
- `Crawler::_check_valid_lane()` ignores a lane file only after it is an hour old. Until then every 10-minute cron run quits with "lane in use", so the crawler works about 5 minutes per hour. The previous full crawl took 9,111 s for about 1,080 pages × 2 crawlers.
- With the lane released and `LITESPEED_CRAWLER_DURATION` set to 240, turns end cleanly and the next cron run continues from the same position.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`: on `plugins_loaded`, when LiteSpeed Cache is loaded (`LSCWP_V`) and `LITESPEED_CRAWLER_DURATION` is not defined, define it as 240. The `seoprostack_litespeed_crawler_duration` filter can change the value; 0 leaves the constant undefined. LiteSpeed Cache reads it only when a crawl starts (`Crawler::get_crawler_duration()`).
- Docblock, setting description, README (Fixes for other plugins; LiteSpeed hosting → the crawler), and changelog lines.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` (phpcs, phpstan).
- Throwaway site with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1: with the fix on, `wp eval 'echo \LiteSpeed\Crawler::cls()->get_crawler_duration();'` gives 240. With the fix off, it gives 900. A constant already in `wp-config.php` is kept.
- Live: the crawler summary shows turns ending with `stopped_maxtime` (not a stale `is_running`), and positions advance on each 10-minute run.

title: feat: Hosting needs checks LiteSpeed Cache's crawler and fixes what stops it, in one click
body:
## What

Hosting needs shows LiteSpeed Cache's crawler status, finds the problems that stop it caching pages, and fixes each in one click through LiteSpeed Cache's own code. This is for sites where LiteSpeed Cache runs on a LiteSpeed server. It appears in the Plugins-screen row and as a Site Health test.

## Why

On a live Hostinger site, the crawler had stopped caching pages and nothing on LiteSpeed Cache's screens said why (#588, #590):

- Server IP was empty behind Cloudflare, so crawler requests went through Cloudflare and failed with 522 timeouts.
- Those failures left pages on the blocklist for good. LiteSpeed Cache never retries a blocklisted page for that crawler, even when it rebuilds the map.
- A crawler turn killed by the host's request limit kept its lane file, so LiteSpeed Cache waited an hour before the next turn.
- People had to work out LiteSpeed Cache's Crawler tabs (Summary, Map, Blocklist, Settings) to find and fix each of these.

## How

New `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php` (`SEOProStack_Litespeed_Crawler`), loaded and booted by Hosting needs (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`, `litespeed_advice()` and `boot()`). It reads LiteSpeed Cache's own API:

- Status: `\LiteSpeed\Crawler::get_summary()`, `list_crawlers()`, `get_crawler_duration()`, lane file `json_local_path() . '.pid'`.
- Stopped turn: the lane file is older than the turn length + 5 minutes. Fix: `Release_lane()`, then start.
- Failed pages: `\LiteSpeed\Crawler_Map::list_blacklist()` rows with `B` (not `N`, which marks pages that can't be cached). Fix: `blacklist_del()`.
- Server IP: `server_ip` is empty, `$_SERVER['SERVER_ADDR']` is public, and the site's host name resolves elsewhere. Fix: a test request to that address with `CURLOPT_RESOLVE` (through `http_api_curl`) must reach LiteSpeed and not Cloudflare. Only then is it saved with `\LiteSpeed\Conf::update_confs()`. On Hostinger, `SERVER_ADDR` equals the origin IP that worked.
- Not running: a crawl in progress whose last turn started over an hour ago. Shortcuts: **Crawl now** (`\LiteSpeed\Task::async_call('crawler_force')`, as LiteSpeed Cache's own button does) and a link to its Crawler screen.

Actions go through `admin-post.php` with a nonce per action, for `manage_options`. Results show as a one-time notice (`removable_query_args`). Nothing is stored. The Hosting needs row allows more than one link per line.

Docs: README (Hosting needs; LiteSpeed hosting → the crawler), `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`, `scripts/preflight-plugin.sh`.
- Throwaway site with LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1 and a simulated LiteSpeed server: the row and the Site Health test render with no PHP messages; seeded `B` and `N` blocklist rows are reported, and only the `B` rows are retried.
- After release, on augustawards.com (Hostinger, behind Cloudflare): the row shows status; with Server IP emptied, the fix link sets it back after its test request; **Crawl now** starts a turn.

title: fix: Hosting needs says the crawler has not crawled yet right after Crawl now
body:
## What

After **Crawl now** on a finished crawl, Hosting needs says "LiteSpeed Cache's crawler is on and has not crawled yet", and the notice says the crawler "has started". Neither is right for what LiteSpeed Cache does next.

## Evidence (live, augustawards.com, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1, SEO Pro Stack 1.3.19)

- Before: `done=touchedEnd`, last start 3,608 s ago.
- After Crawl now: `last_start_time` 45 s ago, `done=0`, `this_full_beginning_time=0`, `end_reason=stopped_reset`.
- Cause, in `litespeed-cache/src`:
  - A manual run after `touchedEnd` runs `Crawler_Map::gen()`, which calls `Crawler::reset_pos()` (crawler-map.cls.php:616). That writes the `.reset` file.
  - The same turn's 5-second check finds the file, zeroes the position and `this_full_beginning_time`, and stops with `stopped_reset` (crawler.cls.php:917-929).
  - The next WP-Cron run (within 10 minutes) does the crawling.
- `status_text()` in `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php` treats `this_full_beginning_time=0` as "never crawled".

## How

`includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed-crawler.php`:

- `status_text()`: when `this_full_beginning_time` is 0 but `last_start_time` is set and the crawl isn't finished, say a full crawl of N pages is starting and WP-Cron runs its next turn within 10 minutes.
- `notice()` (`crawl` and `release`): say the crawler rebuilds its list of pages first and caches them in turns from the next WP-Cron run.
- Docs: README Hosting needs → LiteSpeed Cache's crawler; changelog.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh`.
- Throwaway: seed `this_full_beginning_time=0`, a recent `last_start_time`, `done=0`; the Site Health test shows the new line.
- Live after release: Crawl now, then the row shows the starting text, then progress after the next cron turn.

title: Load plugins only where needed: admin bookkeeping writes reset what the site's pages learned
body:
## Problem

On a live site (LiteSpeed, 51 active plugins), "Load plugins only where needed" kept losing what it learned about the site's pages, so Hosting needs said "has not learned the site's pages yet" and pages that reach PHP (including every LiteSpeed Cache crawler miss) loaded every plugin. A full crawl of 1,017 pages learned the page kinds, but `seoprostack_plugin_front['kinds']` was empty again hours later.

The reset record (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::FRONT_FORGETS`, last 20) showed bookkeeping writes, not content or settings changes, as the causes:

| Cause | Count | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `updated_option _wp_suggested_policy_text_has_changed` via ajax / admin POST | 12 | WordPress core's privacy-policy flag, flipped by `WP_Privacy_Policy_Content::text_change_check()` as admin screens load |
| `updated_post_meta _edit_lock` via ajax | 2 | the editor's post lock, refreshed by Heartbeat while a post is open |
| `updated_option edd_sl_<md5>` via cli / admin GET | 2 | EDD Software Licensing's cached update and licence data for a plugin using its updater |
| `updated_option fs_api_cache` via cli | 1 | Freemius's API cache |
| `updated_option seoprostack_options` via ajax | 2 | real setting changes (correct) |

None of these changes what a public page shows, but each one drops every learned page kind (`forget_front()`), so the crawler's learning lasts only until the next admin visit.

## Fix

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: add the bookkeeping options to `RECORD_OPTIONS` (`_wp_suggested_policy_text_has_changed`, `edd_sl_` prefix, `fs_api_cache`), and skip editor locks (`_edit_lock`, `_edit_last`) in `post_meta_changed()`. Saving a post still forgets through `save_post`.
- Docs: `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt` and `README.md` Unreleased.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`.
- Throwaway site: learn a page kind, then flip `_wp_suggested_policy_text_has_changed`, write `_edit_lock` and an `edd_sl_` option through an admin AJAX request: `kinds` stays; `save_post` still resets.
- Live after release: reset record over a day of normal admin use, and `kinds` filling during the next crawl.

title: Fixes for other plugins: stop dbDelta() altering unchanged enum columns on every call (Tutor LMS Pro notifications table)
body:
## What happens

WordPress 6.9 and later (checked in 7.1.3 and in `trunk`) compares each existing column's type with a **lowercased** copy of the type in a plugin's `CREATE TABLE` statement, in `dbDelta()` (`wp-admin/includes/upgrade.php`):

```php
$fieldtype_lowercased = strtolower( $fieldtype );
...
if ( $tablefield->Type !== $fieldtype_lowercased ) {
```

WordPress 6.8 compared `$tablefield->Type !== $fieldtype`. The database reports `enum` and `set` values in the case they were created with, so a column such as `` `status` enum('READ','UNREAD') `` always looks changed, and `dbDelta()` runs `ALTER TABLE … CHANGE COLUMN` for it every time it is called.

Tutor LMS Pro 4.1.0 calls `dbDelta()` for `{prefix}tutor_notifications` on every request (`addons/tutor-notifications/classes/Init.php`, `create_notifications_db_table()`). On a live site, admin profiling showed `ALTER TABLE wp_tutor_notifications CHANGE COLUMN `status` `status` enum('READ','UNREAD')` on every admin screen and admin-ajax request, at 40–116 ms each. `dbDelta($sql, false)` reports: `Changed type of wp_tutor_notifications.status from enum('READ','UNREAD') to enum('READ','UNREAD')`.

## Fix

Add it to **Fixes for other plugins** (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-fixes.php`), on the `dbdelta_create_queries` filter, which that class already uses for Tutor LMS (`tutor_create_queries()`):

- Only for a `CREATE TABLE` statement whose table exists.
- For each `enum`/`set` column line with upper-case letters: if the table's column type is the same, byte for byte, and the line sets nothing else that differs (only `NULL`/`NOT NULL`, matching the column), drop that line from the statement. `dbDelta()` never drops columns that a statement leaves out, so nothing else changes. A real change (a new value, another case) is kept and runs as before. New tables are created as written.
- Document it in the class header, the setting's description, README.md (Fixes for other plugins) and the changelogs.

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`.
- Throwaway WordPress 7.1 site: create a table with an upper-case `enum`, then call `dbDelta()` with the same statement. Before: an `ALTER` runs each time. After: none. Change the enum's values: the `ALTER` still runs. A new table is still created.
- Live: after release, the admin profile no longer shows the `ALTER TABLE wp_tutor_notifications` query.

title: Database character set: Site Health check and on-request utf8mb4 conversion
body:
## What

On a live site, 15 tables (`wp_options`, `wp_posts`, `wp_postmeta`, users, comments, terms and a few plugin tables) were still `utf8mb3_general_ci`, while the other 281 tables and WordPress's connection were `utf8mb4`. Any 4-byte character, such as an emoji, failed to save to options and meta. Kadence Blocks 3.7.12.1 lost its Harbor product catalog that way (`lw_harbor_catalog_state`, one 🎉 in a 110 KB value), and Rank Math descriptions or block settings with an emoji fail the same way, silently. WordPress only converts its tables in the 4.2 upgrade, so sites moved later from an older database keep `utf8mb3` for good.

Converting the tables by hand (backup, then `ALTER TABLE … CONVERT TO CHARACTER SET utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci`, one table at a time) fixed it: `wp_postmeta` (588k rows, 240 MB) took 35 s, `wp_posts` 9 s, the rest under a second.

## Plan

New feature `SEOProStack_Database_Charset` (Server tab), modelled on `SEOProStack_Database_Keys`:

- **Site Health test, always on** (advice only): tables of this site that cannot store emoji (`utf8`/`utf8mb3`, or any text column in those), read with `SHOW TABLE STATUS` and `SHOW FULL COLUMNS` (on the live site an `information_schema.COLUMNS` query timed out). Tables in another character set (such as `latin1`) are listed, never converted: they may hold mis-encoded text that converting would garble.
- **Fix, off by default** (changes the database; `AGENTS.md`): Tools → Database character set lists those tables with rows and size, and converts one table (or every eligible one) on a nonce-checked POST, after a back-up warning. Target collation: the connection's (`$wpdb->collate`) when it is `utf8mb4`, else the most common `utf8mb4` collation among the site's tables, so joins never meet "Illegal mix of collations" (GitHub issue #550). Never waits for a table lock (`lock_wait_timeout`), one conversion at a time (`GET_LOCK`), logged with autoload off; uninstall removes the log.
- `wp seoprostack charset list|convert` for large tables, which may outlast a web request.

### Files Scope

- NEW: `includes/features/class-seoprostack-database-charset.php`
- EDIT: `includes/class-seoprostack-setup.php`
- EDIT: `uninstall.php`
- EDIT: `README.md`
- EDIT: `readme.txt`
- EDIT: `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `bash scripts/lint.sh`; `scripts/plugin-check.sh` (after committing).
- Throwaway site: convert `wp_options` and `wp_postmeta` to `utf8mb3_general_ci`; Site Health reports them; `update_option()` with an emoji fails; convert from Tools and with WP-CLI; Site Health is good; the emoji saves and reads back; the debug log is empty.

<!-- aidevops:origin:interactive -->
