title: fix: Load plugins only where needed: an update check after a plugin update runs with every plugin
body:
<!-- aidevops:brief-schema=v2 -->

# Load plugins only where needed: an update check after a plugin update runs with every plugin

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-10-07
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (owner session)
- **Conversation context:** On a live site the admin bar showed 3 updates on Pages, while Dashboard > Updates listed none. Correct update counts (#535) was on.

## What

When an update check is due, the loader loads every plugin on that admin request (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::update_check_due()`, reason `updates`, #535). It does so at most once an hour, so sites where checks never run do not load every plugin on every screen. But updating a plugin deletes WordPress's saved plugin check (`wp_clean_plugins_cache()`), so a check is due again straight away. Inside that hour, the next screen that skips plugins runs core's `_maybe_update_plugins()` without them. Plugins that adjust the check while it runs are missing, so the saved check holds offers they would remove and lacks offers they would add.

Change: the hourly limit applies only when the last full load for updates did not leave the checks done (checks switched off or never run there). When the checks ran on that request, the limit is cleared, so the next due check also loads every plugin.

## Why (evidence from the live site)

- 15:58 full load for updates (`seoprostack_plugin_updates_full`); 16:04 SEO Pro Stack 1.3.23 update deleted the check; the next check ran on a skipping screen.
- Reproduced with WP-CLI: the same check with every plugin offers 0 updates; with the plugins Pages loads (Rank Math, Kadence Blocks, Admin Columns Pro, WP Sheet Editor, plus the always-loaded ones) it offers WooCommerce GoCardless 3.0.3 (WordPress.org) and WooCommerce Subscriptions 9.3.0. Installed versions equal the checked ones, so Correct update counts counts them as real; opening Updates re-checks with every plugin and lists none.

## How

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php` `update_check_due()` (around line 527): split the due test from the hourly limit; on an `updates` request, after core's checks on `admin_init`, clear `UPDATES_FULL` when no check is still due.
- `EDIT: changelog.txt`, `README.md` (changelog), `readme.txt` (newest changelog).

### Hazards

- `STANDARDS.md` → Code rules: do not change update checks or transients; this only loads more plugins. Never name the update transient filters in code or comments (Plugin Check `plugin_updater_detected`).

## Acceptance

- After a plugin update within an hour of a full load for updates, the next admin screen loads every plugin (admin bar reason `updates`) and the saved check matches a check with every plugin.
- On a site where checks never run, screens still load every plugin at most once an hour.
- `composer` lint/PHPStan pass.

title: Hosting needs: recommend LiteSpeed Cache's Cache WP-Admin while its object cache works
body:
## What

Hosting needs should recommend LiteSpeed Cache's **Cache WP-Admin** (LiteSpeed Cache → Cache → Object) while LiteSpeed Cache's object cache works, with a one-click action, and take care that admin screens do not show stale data.

## Why

With Cache WP-Admin off, LiteSpeed Cache's object cache reads only transients on admin screens (`_can_cache()` in `src/object-cache.cls.php`, LiteSpeed Cache 7.9.1) and asks the database for everything else. Writes and deletes still go to the cache, so the cache stays as current as the database, and turning it on shows admin screens what the site's pages already read.

Evidence (Hostinger, 2026-10-07):

- A/B on one site: Pages screen median about 2.0 s off against 1.4 s on. Noisy: dashboard changed little.
- 18 of 26 sites on the account already ran with it on; 8 had it off and were turned on with `wp litespeed-option set object-admin true`. On each, a value added, updated and deleted through the options API read the same from the object cache and the database.

## Care with stale data

- Recommend only while the daily object cache check finds LiteSpeed Cache's cache **working**.
- The action re-checks: stored result working, `wp_using_ext_object_cache()`, PHP extension loaded and the server answering, then saves only `object-admin` through LiteSpeed Cache's own code (network settings when network-active), which rewrites `.litespeed_conf.dat`. Changing `object-admin` does not trigger a Purge All (`_conf_purge_all()` covers only cache, ESI, debug and network-primary settings).
- Text says changes made outside WordPress (database tool, restore, SQL import) need Toolbox → Purge All, as they already do for the site's pages.
- With it on and the cache unreachable: advise Purge All once the cache answers again, since deletes made meanwhile never reached it.
- SEO Pro Stack's own direct writes to core tables were checked: each clears the object cache copy (`clean_post_cache`, `clean_term_cache`, `wp_cache_delete`), or only touches rows with no cached parent.

## Files

- `includes/class-seoprostack-litespeed.php`: `admin_cache()`, `save_admin_cache()`, shared `save_object_settings()` used by `save_object_cache()`.
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-hosting-needs.php`: `ADMIN_CACHE` admin-post action, `admin_cache_advice()`, `turn_on_admin_cache()`, notice in `fix_notice()`.
- `README.md` (Hosting needs), `changelog.txt` and `readme.txt` (Unreleased).

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- On a LiteSpeed site with the object cache working and Cache WP-Admin off: the Plugins screen's Hosting needs row shows the recommendation and link; clicking it turns the setting on (`wp litespeed-option get object-admin` returns 1, `.litespeed_conf.dat` has `"object-admin":true`), and the recommendation goes.

title: Load plugins only where needed: login-time hooks no longer make a plugin load on every admin screen
body:
## What

Load plugins only where needed: plugins that only check logins, registrations or lost passwords, or set login cookies, should no longer load on every admin screen.

## Why

`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::sensitive_plugins()` builds the admin map's `always` list from the loader's `ALWAYS_HOOKS` plus the site's `FRONT_ALWAYS_HOOKS` and `FRONT_LOGIN_HOOKS`. Admin screens that skip plugins are only GET/HEAD views by someone already logged in (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::filterable_request()` / `view_request()`: no form, action, nonce, AJAX, REST, cron or network admin). On those, `authenticate`, `wp_authenticate_user`, `wp_login`, `wp_login_failed`, `login_init`, `login_form`, `registration_errors`, `lostpassword_post`, XML-RPC and REST auth hooks never run, and core never calls `wp_set_auth_cookie()` (the only user of `auth_cookie_expiration`, `secure_auth_cookie`, `secure_logged_in_cookie`; `auth_cookie` is in `wp_generate_auth_cookie()`). wp-login.php, saves, XML-RPC and REST load every plugin, so a login can never skip a two-factor, CAPTCHA or login-limit plugin.

Evidence, one Hostinger site (51 active plugins), 2026-10-07: 14 plugins loaded on every admin screen. Five were there only through login-time hooks: Tutor LMS Pro (spam protection, email verification, 2FA at login), Really Simple Security Pro (2FA, CAPTCHA, login limits, login cookie lifetime), FluentCRM (`wp_login` tracking), Simple Cloudflare Turnstile and Secure Custom Fields (`registration_errors`). Tutor LMS Pro and FluentCRM are among the heavier plugins on that site's admin screens.

## Kept on every admin screen

- `ALWAYS_HOOKS`: `login_url`, `auth_redirect`, `option_active_plugins`, `pre_option_active_plugins`.
- New `ADMIN_ALWAYS_HOOKS`: `determine_current_user` (who is logged in), `session_token_manager` (where sessions are kept; skipping a replacement would log people out), `logout_url` (the admin bar's log out link on every screen).
- `PERMISSION_HOOKS` (`user_has_cap`, `map_meta_cap`, `role_has_cap`, `editable_roles`, `determine_current_user`): unchanged. Some plugins restrict capabilities there (WooCommerce's shop manager limits), and grants cannot be told from restrictions, so skipping one could widen access.

The site's own lists (`FRONT_ALWAYS_HOOKS`, `FRONT_LOGIN_HOOKS`) are unchanged.

## Files

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`: `ADMIN_ALWAYS_HOOKS`, `sensitive_plugins()`, label in `plugin_options()`.
- `includes/class-seoprostack-plugin-loader.php`: `MAP_VERSION` 10 → 11, so every screen learns again with the new list (screens learned while these plugins always loaded do not list them where they are used).
- `README.md`, `changelog.txt`, `readme.txt`.

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh php phpcs phpstan`.
- After deploy on that site: the map's `always` list (`seoprostack_plugin_map`) no longer holds the five plugins; Dashboard and Pages load fewer plugins (admin bar Plugins count); profile screens still show Really Simple Security's and Tutor's 2FA fields (learned from the profile screen); logging in with 2FA and CAPTCHA still works (wp-login.php loads every plugin); no new debug log messages from those plugins.

title: Admin screens respond immediately to clicks while the next screen loads
body:
## What

When Preload pages → **Also in the admin** is on, clicking a link to another admin screen responds immediately: the admin menu highlights the new screen and the content area shows a placeholder with its title while the page loads. Supporting browsers fade between screens while the admin menu and admin bar stay still.

## Why

Measured on a live site (augustawards.com, 50 active plugins, 1.3.27, signed in, Chromium), warm loads: the server takes 0.65–3.8 s per admin screen, the browser 0.1–0.5 s after the page arrives. Until the next page arrives, nothing on screen changes after a click, so even fast screens feel slow. Hover prefetch (#625) already cuts click-to-load from about 3.2 s to 1 s when the pointer rests on a link; this covers the clicks it cannot.

Swapping only the content area without loading the page (as Fluent Boards, Bookings and Support do inside their own screens) would break plugins across the admin: each screen loads its own scripts and styles, and plugins expect a fresh page. This change keeps normal page loads and only changes what is shown while waiting.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-preload-pages.php`: with `preload_pages_admin` on, print a small inline script (`wp_print_inline_script_tag()`) and style on admin screens.
- Script: on a plain left click on a same-site admin link, remember the link; on `beforeunload`, if no other handler asked to confirm leaving (unsaved changes), mark the menu item current and, after 100 ms, hide the content area's children and show a placeholder (title from the menu, `role="status"`). Undo on `pageshow` from the back-forward cache and after 30 s. Skip new-tab, download and export links, admin-ajax.php, admin-post.php and async-upload.php, and hash links to the same screen.
- Style: `@view-transition { navigation: auto; }` with `view-transition-name` on the admin menu and admin bar, a short fade, off with reduced motion. The placeholder uses `currentColor` so it fits admin colour schemes.

## Verify

- On the preview site (`scripts/preview-site.sh`), in Chromium: clicking a menu item highlights it and shows the placeholder within one frame; the screen then loads normally.
- Leaving an edited post asks to confirm as before, and choosing to stay leaves the screen unchanged.
- Back and forward buttons show the real screens, not the placeholder.
- No console errors; `scripts/lint.sh`, PHPCS and PHPStan pass.
- Also: find what takes 2–4 s on the server on Plugins and Settings on the live site; file follow-ups for anything fixable.

title: Plugins screen: cut SEO Pro Stack's own cost (starter data queries, size column, menu copy)
body:
## What

On a live site with about 50 active plugins, SEO Pro Stack's own work on the Plugins screen (`plugins.php`) costs about 376 ms and 111 database queries out of a 3.7 s screen (warm, fastest of 3 runs, temporary per-callback profiler, now removed). Three parts are worth cutting:

| Where | Cost per Plugins screen |
|---|---|
| Starter data links and row meta (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Presets::action_links()` / `row_meta()` → `SEOProStack_Starters::missing_count()` and `missing()`) | ~50 ms; ~105 queries such as `select * from wp_fc_tags where slug = ? LIMIT ?` (54x), `wp_fc_lists` (28x), `wp_fc_meta` (12x), `wp_fluentform_forms` (8x) |
| Size column (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Sizes::render_column()`) | ~164 ms, all cached sizes (no measuring) |
| Admin menu copy on screens that load every plugin (`SEOProStack_Plugin_Loading::capture_menu()`) | 58–75 ms, also on Settings |

## Why

The Plugins screen is one of the slowest admin screens (#631 makes the wait visible; this cuts it). These are SEO Pro Stack's own costs, so they are ours to fix.

## How

1. **Starter data (clear fix).** `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-presets.php`: `starter_links()` (line ~316) calls `SEOProStack_Starters::missing_count($slug)` and `starter_meta()` (line ~350) calls `SEOProStack_Starters::missing($slug)`; both run `SEOProStack_Starters::exists()` (`includes/class-seoprostack-starters.php`, ~715) for every item, so each row repeats the same lookups. Work out each slug's missing items once per request (static memo in `SEOProStack_Starters`, keyed by slug, cleared after starter-add/remove in the same request) and derive the count from it if `missing_count()`'s `when`/`requirement_met()` rules allow; otherwise memoise each separately.
2. **Size column (measure first).** In `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-sizes.php`, time `opcache()` (`opcache_get_status(true)` lists every cached script on the server; on shared hosting that can be tens of thousands), `cost_line()` / `SEOProStack_Plugin_Cost::line()` per row, and `cell()`. Fix whichever dominates, for example reading the OPcache script list only when that cell is shown or caching the per-plugin totals briefly. Keep the numbers current (owner's wish: no stale results).
3. **Menu copy (optional).** `capture_menu()` (`includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` ~999) resolves the owner of every page callback with `SEOProStack_Plugin_Loader::plugin_for_callback()` in `page_owners()` (~1162). If reflection dominates, memoise callback → plugin per request. Do not capture less often: the copy must stay fresh.

## Acceptance

- Plugins screen with presets and starter data shown: the per-row starter queries run once per slug, and the rows show the same links and status as before.
- Size column shows the same sizes, OPcache figures and page-time lines.
- `scripts/lint.sh` passes. Note before/after timings in the PR (Query Monitor or the server's timing on a test site with FluentCRM and Fluent Forms active).

## Context

Measured 2026-10-08 on a production site; host and profile files kept out of this issue. Related: #626 (Kadence and Tutor LMS costs), #631 (click response while screens load).

title: Short addresses: let other plugins add their post types (seoprostack_short_address_types)
body:
## What

Let other plugins serve their own post types at short addresses (`/item/` instead of `/base/item/`) through Short addresses for custom post types, with a new filter `seoprostack_short_address_types`. SEO Pro Directory uses it for its per-directory "Short addresses" setting (wpallstars/seoprodirectory), so a directory's listings are served at `/name/` without the site owner also ticking the post type here.

## Why

A plugin that registers a post type knows best whether its items should have short addresses, and lets its users choose that where they set the type up. Today the only way is this feature's own post-type list, so the directory plugin would have to write into SEO Pro Stack's settings (two sources of truth) or ask users to set it in two places.

## How

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-remove-cpt-base.php`:
  - `types()`: start from the chosen types when the feature is on (else none), then `apply_filters('seoprostack_short_address_types', $types)`; keep the existing checks (pretty permalinks, `post_type_exists()`, fixed base via `prefix()`), de-duplicate.
  - `boot()`: keep hooking at once when switched on; otherwise hook `init` (priority 1) and add the link, request and redirect hooks only when the filter has callbacks, so a site without either pays nothing.
  - `panel_status()`: show the clashing-addresses list whenever `types()` is not empty (not only when switched on), and list the post types other plugins added: "Other plugins also serve these at short addresses: …".
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php` `front_routes()`: `short_types` from `types()` alone (it now covers the switch).
- `README.md` (feature section and Extending → Filters), `readme.txt` and `changelog.txt` (Unreleased).

### Files Scope

- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-remove-cpt-base.php`
- `includes/features/class-seoprostack-plugin-loading.php`
- `README.md`
- `readme.txt`
- `changelog.txt`

## Verification

- `scripts/lint.sh` passes.
- Disposable WordPress with a test plugin that registers `book` (rewrite slug `library`) and adds it with the filter, feature switched off: `/library/x/` redirects (301) to `/x/`, `/x/` is the book, `get_permalink()` is `/x/`; a page named `x` keeps `/x/` and the book keeps `/library/x/`. Without the filter callback, nothing changes and no hooks are added. With the feature on and another type chosen, both types work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A post type added only through the filter gets short addresses, redirects and clash handling, with the feature switched on or off.
- With no filter callbacks and the feature off, no link, request or redirect hooks are added (no new per-request cost).
- The settings panel names post types added by other plugins.
